title: Backup your experimental data
wikitext:
==== Authentification forwarding ==== First of all: log in to your experiment server via ssh using the -A flag.
This enables authentication forwarding. Don't use it always. : 
ssh -A @
''in addition, you may have to use a jumphost (-J sshgate.upb.de or -J jump.aksw.uni-leipzig.de)'' ==== Copying ==== Now you can copy it to hobbit-data: * You can copy to your home-folder : 
scp -r testfile @hobbitdata.aksw.uni-leipzig.de:~
* Or to some backup directory: : 
scp -r testfile @hobbitdata.aksw.uni-leipzig.de:/data/backups/-DD-MM-YYYY
''please name your files in that folder by the scheme: -DD-MM-YYYY'' ==== Beam your data ==== See https://git.cs.uni-paderborn.de/ag-ngonga/beam for the source code and instructions on building, installing and updating beam. The experiment servers have a tool called beam installed. This tool can be used to compress and upload a folder and later download and decompress it. The advantage of beam is that it does not need to create a temporary file during upload or download (in contrast to manually creating a compressed archive with tar and then uploading that), allowing uploading even if the compressed archive would not fit on the disk at the same time as the uncompressed files. To upload a folder use: : 
beam up
This will create and upload a file with a name like folder-timestamp.tar.zstd. To download a file use : 
beam down
To see available files use : 
beam list
This will download and extract the folder in the current working directory. Finally you should use : 
beam delete
to delete any files you uploaded and no longer need.

title: CKAN
wikitext:
== DICE CKAN == To get the DICE datasets indexed online, you can use the '''[https://ckan.dice-research.org/ CKAN (DICE datasets metadata)]'''. There are search engines for datasets, e.g. [https://datasetsearch.research.google.com/ Google Dataset Search], through which records can be found. The CKAN can be used to make datasets (and related papers) public to the research community. For example, a [https://datasetsearch.research.google.com/search?query=open%20license%20attributes query for open license attributes] will provide a link to a DICE paper and a [https://datasetsearch.research.google.com/search?query=mobility%20metadata query for mobility metadata] will provide a link to one of our projects. == Adding and editing datasets manually == * The CKAN is only used for providing metadata, not the data itself. Data can e.g. be published via [https://wikis.uni-paderborn.de/dice/DiceResources#FTP_Server hobbitdata FTP]. You can use the directory ''/public/CKAN'', which is available at [https://hobbitdata.informatik.uni-leipzig.de/CKAN/ here]. * You can log in with the user dice and password GuMvFGRd0GquLXzn. To add a dataset, go to ''Datasets'' -> ''Add Dataset''. * If you want to publish multiple related files, consider creating one dataset entry and several resource entries (see below). === Dataset fields === * '''Title''': Use a short description including the most relevant search terms. A description of the data contents is better than e.g. a project acronym. * '''Publisher URI''': Default is ''https://dice-research.org/'', that will e.g. be used as an URI for graphs. * '''Description''': Include relevant search terms for your data contents. You can also provide additional information like related research articles. You could use markdown formatting, but plain text is recommended as the metadata is shared and used in different ways. * '''Tags''': Use popular and specific tags. * '''License''': A good choice is ''Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0'', where people can use the data for open projects, but have to cite DICE. * '''Organization''': DICE * '''Visibility''': Can be set to ''private'' until you're sure the final metadata is complete. Afterwards set it to ''public''. * '''Source''': Optional, if you already provide the data at another source. * '''Version''': This is up to you. Using just ''1.0'' is fine. * '''Author/Maintainer/Email''': Please set at least one author or maintainer name. If you have no concerns about spam, set you email address. But be aware the metadata is probably published at several public repositories. === Resource fields === * '''Data''': An URL of an existing, publicly available file. If you did not upload a file yet, see ''FTP'' above. * '''Size''': Required field. Determine and set the file size in bytes. * '''Name''': If you provide several resources, use this field highlight specifics to make differences to other files clear. * '''Description''': More specific/detailed information than in field name. * '''Format''': Will be guessed automatically. Leave blank if you wish. == Adding and editing datasets using the CKAN API == * The [https://docs.ckan.org/en/2.9/api/ API guide 2.9] is described online. * Some examples are listed at the [https://ckan.dice-research.org/about about page]. * Example scripts are available at https://github.com/dice-group/dice-ckan/tree/dice/scripts === API tokens === * Having several API tokens helps in cases, if one token has to be replaced, e.g. if accidentally uploaded. * Additional API tokens can be generated by user dice at the [https://ckan.dice-research.org/user/dice/api-tokens api-tokens] page. As they are only visible after creation, you can add them below. * API token for the ML group: eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpYXQiOjE2Mjc0MTYxMzQsImp0aSI6IjAzQXQyaWJnWlAzeXFiYlptYXdDdGQxb1VJallscFZzX0t4QWg4VF9OX0MxUWYyMENNb2lBMVRmWDdsZjBwbDV3QWFKN1NKZC1LamtvZkdIIn0.X3HVJPKS2Txt7K0ja_-7SKAJGCLerqqIL8x19PLDHPo == Backup == Simple backups can created by a script and uploaded to FTP, see https://hobbitdata.informatik.uni-leipzig.de/CKAN/CKAN-Backup/ == Development == If you want to test CKAN on your machine, you can use the installation instructions in the [https://github.com/dice-group/dice-ckan dice-ckan] repository. Required steps are 1, 2 and 4.
The VM was created by the infastructure crew, see this [https://git.cs.uni-paderborn.de/dice-infrastructure/issue-tracking/-/issues/153 issue].

title: DBpediaSetup
wikitext:
== Internal DBpedia Setup ==

Current DBpedia instance is provided using Virtuoso with data loaded from [https://databus.dbpedia.org/ DBpedia databus].
The Virtuoso instance was assembled using [https://github.com/dbpedia/dev.dbpedia.org/blob/master/pics/Dockerfile.dockerfile official DBpedia Dockerfile].

=== Building docker image === 

To build the docker image from Dockerfile, the following command was used:

  docker build \
    --build-arg endpoint="https://databus.dbpedia.org/repo/sparql" \
    --build-arg default_graph="http://sparql.uni-paderborn.de:8891/dbpedia" \
    --build-arg buffer_memory="16384" \
    -t databus-dbpedia-virtuoso .

It sets the endpoint to Databus, default graph to our URI and expands buffer memory for virtuoso to 16g.

The following command can be used to run the container once the build is finished:

  docker run -d \
    -p 8891:8890 \
    -p 1112:1111 \
    --name databus-dbpedia-virtuoso \
    -v /data/dbpedia-databus-instance/data:/data \
    databus-dbpedia-virtuoso "$(cat query.sparql)"

This will start the container with a SPARQL query (see below) from `query.sparql` file and import the data from Databus into local Virtuoso instance.
Once import is finished - Virtuoso instance will be started with the imported data.

=== SPARQL query for the data ===

The image built from official Dockerfile expects a SPARQL query that enumerates all the artifacts that need to be downloaded and imported.
Following query was used for current instance:

  PREFIX dataid: <http://dataid.dbpedia.org/ns/core#>
  PREFIX dct: <http://purl.org/dc/terms/>
  PREFIX dcat:  <http://www.w3.org/ns/dcat#>
  SELECT ?file {
    {
      ?dataset dataid:artifact ?artifact .
      ?dataset dataid:version ?latest .
      ?dataset dcat:distribution ?distribution.
      ?distribution dataid:contentVariant 'en'^^<http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string> .
      ?distribution dcat:downloadURL ?file  .
      {
        SELECT ?artifact (max(?version) as ?latest) WHERE {
          ?dataset dataid:group ?group .
          FILTER (?group in (<https://databus.dbpedia.org/dbpedia/generic>, <https://databus.dbpedia.org/dbpedia/generic>, <https://databus.dbpedia.org/dbpedia/mappings> )) .
          ?dataset dataid:artifact ?artifact .
          FILTER (?artifact != <https://databus.dbpedia.org/dbpedia/generic/wikilinks>)
          ?dataset dataid:version ?version .
        } GROUP BY ?artifact order by desc (?artifact)
      }
    } UNION {
      ?dataset dataid:artifact <https://databus.dbpedia.org/dbpedia/ontology/dbo-snapshots> .
      ?dataset dcat:distribution ?distribution .
      ?distribution dcat:downloadURL ?file .
    } 
  } order by desc(?file)

This query gets all the latest DBpedia artifacts for English language.

This tells FTP to open a port on the server instead of the client when transferring data. * You can use lftp -e "set ftp:ssl-protect-data true;" -u hobbit files.dice-research.org to connect * Basic FTP usage in lftp: ** cd public/projects -- change FTP directory ** put myfile.zip -- upload a file from a local directory to the current FTP directory ** get myfile.zip -- download a file ** lcd some/directory -- change a local directory (default is the one where lftp was started) ** mirror -- download the contents of the current FTP directory to the local directory ** mirror -R -- upload the contents of the local directory to the current FTP directory * Certificate validation error (https://github.com/lavv17/lftp/issues/641): try this: lftp -e "set ftp:ssl-protect-data true; set ssl:verify-certificate/93:3C:6D:DE:E9:5C:9C:41:A4:0F:9F:50:49:3D:82:BE:03:AD:87:BF no" -u hobbit files.dice-research.org -- '''Only use exactly this certificate ID of the "ISRG Root X1" certificate.''' * You can also put the following into your "~/.lftprc" instead of passing arguments every time: 
set ftp:ssl-protect-data true
set ssl:verify-certificate/93:3C:6D:DE:E9:5C:9C:41:A4:0F:9F:50:49:3D:82:BE:03:AD:87:BF no # ISRG Root X1
== DICE LLM Chat == We have deployed chat-based LLMs at https://dice-llm-chat.cs.uni-paderborn.de/. You can choose from a list of available models to suit your use case, whether for general tasks, reasoning, or coding. Please find more details here: https://wikis.uni-paderborn.de/dice/LLMs#DICE_LLM_Chat. == Image generation == DICE LLM chat is integrated with an image generation pipeline. == Server hardware == The DICE group can make use of several servers and [[VirtualMachines]] (VMs). The servers owned by the group have different usages and obviously not every server can be used for everything. If you have questions or problems, you can always contact the person in charge of the single servers. === SSH Login === At this point, all of the experiment servers are running a IRB managed debian. This means that you can login with your IMT account. To do so you you can either ssh into the sshgate.cs.upb.de using your password and the ssh to your desired server, or you can setup kerberos using these guides (https://hilfe.uni-paderborn.de/Single-Sign-On_einrichten_unter_Linux and https://hilfe.uni-paderborn.de/Single-Sign-On_einrichten_f%C3%BCr_SSH_und_SCP_(Linux) ) and login to the servers directly. For ssh login do this: 
ssh username@sshgate.cs.uni-paderborn.de ==> "Enter IMT password"

ssh servername ==> "E.g., ssh qilin"
To reload Nvidia drivers, execute this after the login above: 
sudo reload-nvidia-driver.sh
=== Experiment servers === Experiment servers can be used for experiments. '''They have to be booked before hand!''' The booking is done in {{Sciebo|952907499|Sciebo spreadsheet where you can also find up-to-date usage instructions}}. Join the chat room for servers-related chats and announcements: https://matrix.to/#/#dice-server-users:chat.dice-research.org Please read the following rules for booking a server carefully: # The experiment servers are shared resources. It doesn't matter how important or urgent your experiments are: please keep in mind that other members of our group want to use the servers as well. # If a person wants to use a server, e.g., for experiments, he/she has to book the server before starting the experiment. # Booking works by choosing the server from the tabs below and filling in your name into the form. # When your experiment ends, make sure that #* all your processes are stopped. It is very rude to leave something running on the server since most users have not enough priviliges to stop processes of other users. #* all your data is copied to another machine if you would like to keep it (e.g., using the [https://wikis.uni-paderborn.de/dice/Backup_your_experimental_data beam script]). #: '''Note''': The experiment servers might be cleaned and restarted any time between two bookings. # A person can book a server only for a maximum of two consecutive weeks. There are no exceptions! # If the last day of your booked two weeks has been reached and there is no following booking it is fine to create a new booking for the next two weeks. # User accounts/credentials are not to be shared between people. # If you have a conflict with another member of the group because he/she is blocking a server that you have booked, please contact that person and try to solve the issue directly. We are all working on the success of our group and there is no reason why we shouldn't talk to each other ;) '''Failed to initialize NVML: Driver/library version mismatch''': This happens if the NVIDIA driver is updates, but the old version is still loaded. To unload the old version use : sudo rmmod nvidia_drm : sudo rmmod nvidia_modeset : sudo rmmod nvidia_uvm : sudo rmmod nvidia You can also use : sudo reload-nvidia-driver.sh === Server access === Everyone in {{IMT group|ag-ngonga}} has access to all servers as a normal user. People (such as students) can be added to IMT groups dice-SERVERNAME-users (or dice-SERVERNAME-admins) to allow access (with sudo) to specific servers. === Available Servers === [[Server List]] Servers with "Experiment Server" in the column Purpose can be used for experiments. === JupyterHub === The experiment servers have a JupyterHub installed. You can access it at .cs.upb.de. They are available directly from outside of UPB network. The deployment files for the JupyterHub setup can be found here: https://git.cs.uni-paderborn.de/ag-ngonga/jupyterhub-setup ==== JupyterHub troubleshooting ==== * Try to go to https://SERVERNAME.cs.uni-paderborn.de/hub/home and restart your user server. === Experiment server troubleshooting === ==== Checking for concurrent usage ==== Tools like htop and w can be used to check if there are any other user's processes running. Note that it's possible to view command line arguments and some other information this way, so don't put sensitive data into command line arguments. === Jupyterhub is not reachable === Several possible causes - jupyterhub.service stopped. {{Restricted|Fix: sudo systemctl start jupyterhub.service}} ==== Server is not reachable ==== First check if you can connect to the server with ssh from the UPB network. If you can't connect, write a e-mail to {{IRB Contact}} and put infrastructure@dice-research.org in CC. == Providing datasets to the public == You can use the FTP (see above) for providing data and [[CKAN]] for publishing metadata.

title: Docker
wikitext: == Docker == If you have questions or problems, please contact the infrastructure crew. === Basics === Docker has two main concepts called image and container. A image is a template, it should contain everything needed to run an application. A container is a running instance of an image, it can contain working state and other runtime artifacts of an application. === Installation === Follow the official Docker install instructions here: https://docs.docker.com/install/ === Creating a Docker image from your application / demo === ==== Basics ==== A Docker image is created by the Docker daemon following the steps in a Dockerfile. The full documentation of a Dockerfiles syntax can be found here: https://docs.docker.com/engine/reference/builder/ ==== Choosing a base image ==== First of all you have to choose a base image on which to build your own image. For example, if you have a java application you should use the [https://hub.docker.com/_/openjdk OpenJDK] Docker image. There are also images of various Linux Distributions such as [https://hub.docker.com/_/ubuntu Ubuntu] or [https://hub.docker.com/_/debian Debian]. Also choose the right tag for your base image. If your application runs on Java 8, use an image with Java 8 (for example openjdk:8) In the following we will need two different base images: One for the build environment and one for the runtime environment. ==== The build environment ==== In the following we will use the example of a Java application using the Maven build system. The base Image we will use for our build environment will be maven:3-jdk-8. To start our Dockerfile we now write FROM maven:3-jdk-8 AS builder. FROM tells Docker which base image we want to use, the AS builder part assigns the name builder. This will become important later. To build our application we first have to copy our source code into the running container. We do this by writing ADD . /example. This will copy the Docker build context into the folder /example inside the container. Next we will need to change our working directory to the newly created directory containing our application code. We do this by writing WORKDIR /example. Now we need to build our application. In this case, since we are building a maven application, we just need to write RUN mvn package into our Dockerfile. RUN tells Docker to run the given command inside the container. To make the next part easier we will now rename the resulting jar file, by writing RUN mv target/*.jar target/example.jar. ==== The runtime environment ==== To keep the final download size of our image small, we should only add anything needed to run our application. For example, we don't need maven to run our application. In this example we will use openjdk:8 as our base image, so we will write FROM openjdk:8 into our Dockerfile. Next we need to copy the build application from the build environment into the runtime environment. We do this by writing COPY --from=builder /example/target/example.jar /example.jar. This will copy the file /example/target/example.jar from the build environment to the runtime environment at the path /example. Now we just need to tell Docker how to start our application. We do this by writing CMD java -jar /example.jar. The CMD tells Docker to execute the given command to start our application. ==== Building the image ==== Now we have everything in our Dockerfile and are ready to build our image. To do this execute the command sudo docker build . in a terminal. This will tell Docker to build an image using the current directory as build context. If everything went well you should see a message similar to Successfully built b0fe6648c8ff. We can now run the image by running the sudo docker run b0fe6648c8ff command. If your application listens to connections on some port(s) you need to add those to the command, like this sudo docker run -p 8080:8080 b0fe6648c8ff. ==== Publishing images ==== The best way to publish your image is to push it to a Docker registry. You should use the registry integrated with your project's git repository if it's available for free (GitHub does NOT have this for free). Otherwise, you can use IRB's GitLab instance with the following steps: * make sure you are a member of project https://git.cs.uni-paderborn.de/dice-research/images * login to the registry: sudo docker login hub.cs.upb.de (IMT login and an access token you can create at https://git.cs.uni-paderborn.de/-/profile/personal_access_tokens) * set the image name and tag when you're building the image: sudo docker build -t hub.cs.upb.de/dice-research/images/yourproject:1.0 . where 1.0 is the tag ** multiple -t options can be specified to have version spans: sudo docker build -t example:latest -t example:1 -t example:1.3 -t example:1.3.5 . ** an existing image can also be tagged without rebuild with docker tag * push the image to the registry: sudo docker push hub.cs.upb.de/dice-research/images/yourproject:1.0 (for every tag you have created) Since dice-research/images is a shared registry, make sure you name your image according to your project's name. If you need several images, you can introduce another level in the name: hub.cs.upb.de/dice-research/images/yourproject/image1:latest. Alternative registries include RedHats [https://quay.io/ Quay], [https://github.com/features/packages GitHubs Package Repository] or [https://docs.gitlab.com/ce/user/packages/ GitLabs Package Repository]. Avoid Docker Hub as it has demonstrated to be hostile to free projects. === Don't do === * Don't start multiple processes in the same container * Don't use network: host in docker-compose

title: EU project organization
wikitext:
== Template for EU Project Reports ==

You will find a template for reports for EU projects in [https://svn.dice-research.org/closed/projects/template_EU SVN].

== Writing Guidelines ==
* keep report consistent with deliverables submitted in the reporting period
* summarize what is in the deliverable and include meaningful references to the deliverable (meaning don't repeat the deliverable itself) 

== Notes on preparing the report ==

* If this is not the first report in this project, be sure to refer to the Follow-Up Recommendations and Comments from previous reviews. You will find a separate section in the template to respond to the recommendations.
* It has proven to be practical to integrate the work packages into the report as individual tex. files. This way, all partners involved can write for the corresponding work packages and the main document remains more manageable.

title: Fellowships
wikitext:
=Call for Fellows=
*The call for fellows must be coordinated with the UPB Research Unit. [https://www.uni-paderborn.de/person/60978 Katharina Patz] is responsible for this. The call does not have to be published via UPB's normal portal for job advertisements; it can be distributed via the project page and mailing lists, for example. 
*Important! The candidate must submit a declaration with the application ([https://www.sail.nrw/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/Declaration-of-Consent-SAIL-Fellowships-UPB.pdf Example ])
*[https://www.sail.nrw/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/Call-for-Fellows-UPB.pdf Example for a Call for Fellowships]

=Checklist=
*Applications must be collected by Simone, she coordinates the process and also sends out the rejection notices at the end. 
*Axel has to select suitable applicants, Simone coordinates the interviews. It is best if other people are present at the interview. Please note: The interview must be documented. We must provide Katharina Patz with a signed statement explaining the selection process. This is intended to guarantee that scholarships are not awarded arbitrarily, but are transparent based on criteria. It must contain: List of applicants, selection criteria for the interviews, decision criteria in the interview, reasons for decision. She also needs a declaration from us that the Fellow will be provided with the necessary infrastructure and a workplace. 
*Once a candidate has been selected, an approval document must be prepared. (See [https://svn.dice-research.org/closed/projects/2022/SAIL/Work%20Packages/WP%203%20Network%20Expansion/EXAMPLE%20SAIL%20Fellowship%20Approval%20notice.docx Example here]). This document is then sent to Katharina Patz, who officially offers the scholarship to the candidate. This document specifies:
**The monthly rate of the scholarship: The best way to do this is to use the [https://www.dfg.de/resource/blob/323036/2f7e7eb3e4110dd63ae9bad50a3602e4/60-12-2024-de-data.pdf DFG table for personnel rates] as a guide. Nevertheless, the selected candidate must submit salary statements for the last 3 months. On the one hand, this should show that he or she is in an employment relationship and, on the other hand, this salary can also be included in the considerations for the potential scholarship rate.
**The period of the scholarship
**The objectives of the scholarship, i.e. the rights and obligations of the candidate
*Make sure that you leave enough time for the bureaucratic process and, if necessary, the visa application. Set the start date of the scholarship accordingly so that there is still a bit of a time buffer.
*The candidate must then complete a declaration stating that he or she wishes to take up the scholarship with the rights and obligations agreed in the Approval Notice. See an [https://svn.dice-research.org/closed/projects/2022/SAIL/Work%20Packages/WP%203%20Network%20Expansion/EXAMPLE%20Declaration%20of%20Acceptance%20of%20MKW%20NRW%20Fellowship.docx example of the declaration here].

title: Further education
wikitext:
==Offerings of Paderborn University==

===General Overview===
*'''Jenny Aloni Center for Early-Career Researchers:''' As the central umbrella organization for doctoral students, postdocs and junior professors at Paderborn University, the Jenny Aloni Center provides target group-specific information, training and qualification opportunities and advisory services. Together with the university’s faculty graduate centers, they provide the best possible support on the path to a career in academia, industry or society. [https://www.uni-paderborn.de/en/jennyalonicenter Further information]

===Scientific Training===
*'''Writing Center “Kompetenzzentrum Schreiben”:''' Various offers such as individual writing consultation, online offers and workshops, e.g. "Starting a doctoral project”, "Revision strategies for doctoral students" or "Dealing with peer reviews". Please note: “Kompetenzzentrum Schreiben” offers writing consultations and some of their workshops in English. They also give feedback on English academic texts. Everything else is held in German. : [https://www.uni-paderborn.de/en/university/kompetenzzentrum-schreiben Further information]
*'''Centre for Language Studies (ZfS):''' various workshops in English, e.g. Academic Writing in English, Presentation Skills or Academic Writing Meetups. [https://www.uni-paderborn.de/zfs/sprachenlernen/sprachkurse-fuer-mitarbeiter Further information]
*'''Studium Generale:''' Courses, some of them specifically for international students and scientists, e.g. Presenting and discussing in studies and profession. Seminar for international students and scientists of technical and economic subjects", "Reading, understanding and evaluating texts systematically. Seminar for international students and scientists of technical subjects" or "ProGRess - Resourcefulness against Procrastination." [https://bit.ly/3F8kvEj Further information and course catalog]
*'''Didactic Support: Higher Education Development Unit (HEDU) for Innovation in Education and University Didactics:''' advanced training and consulting offerings in higher education didactics as well as certificate program "Professional Teaching Competency for Higher Education". Course program usually held in German. [https://www.uni-paderborn.de/en/teaching/qualification-and-service/higher-education-development-unit-hedu-for-innovation-in-education-and-university-didactics Further information]

===Languages===
*'''Centre for Language Studies (ZfS):''' Language courses for employees, e.g. English, Spanish or Chinese. [https://www.uni-paderborn.de/zfs/sprachenlernen/sprachkurse-fuer-mitarbeiter Further information and course program]
*'''German for international employees''' This course program is also offered by the Centre for Language Studies (Zentrum für Sprachlehre (ZfS). [https://www.uni-paderborn.de/en/zfs/neu-zentrum-fuer-sprachlehre-zfs/sprachkurse-fuer-mitarbeitende/deutsch Further information and course program]
*'''Self-study center of the ZfS:''' In the media library and the “SPRECHraum” of the ZfS, students, staff and guest students can improve their language skills in self-study with print media, language learning programs and various audio materials. Support is provided by the language learning advisor. [https://www.uni-paderborn.de/en/zfs/media-center Further information]

===Soft skills and career planning===
*'''Internal Continuing Education programme:''' Personnel development offerings for employees, e.g., development of leadership skills, time management, conflict management, career planning, presentation techniques, etc. Some offerings are held in English, e.g. "Pursuing an Academic Career in Germany", "Effective and Dynamic Scientific Presentations - Online and in Person" or "Self-Marketing and Networking in Science". [https://www.uni-paderborn.de/en/zv/4-5/staff-development/continuing-education-and-training Further information and course offerings]
*'''Mentoring program for female doctoral students:''' The goal of the Paderborn Mentoring Program is to help female doctoral students advance during their doctoral studies and to network across disciplines. The program makes it possible to learn about, concretize, and closely examine the options for a career in science and academia with the help of the inside view of experienced female mentors. It provides knowledge about career success strategies and supports professional networking. The program is usually held in German. [https://www.uni-paderborn.de/en/university/mentoring-for-female-doctoral-students Further information and course offerings]
*'''Career Service:''' Various workshops (usually held in German), e.g. Time management, Conflict management or Coding Dojo. [https://zsb.uni-paderborn.de/career-service/veranstaltungsprogramm Further information]
*'''Certificate Program Qualification for Occupational Fields in Business and Society:''' The NRW Certificate Program is intended to help prepare for occupational fields outside the university. This includes activities in business and society, but also activities at universities of applied sciences and non-university research institutions. The workshop program teaches key competencies in the areas of leadership, management, communication and methods. The program is primarily aimed at postdocs. By arrangement, advanced doctoral students and other scientific staff or employees in science management can also participate. (Program is usually held in German) [https://www.uni-paderborn.de/zv/4-5/personalentwicklung/fort-und-weiterbildung/nrw-zertifikat Further information]

===Health===
*'''University sports “Hochschulsport”:''' Various courses, each offered during the lecture period and lecture-free periods (subject to a fee), e.g. Meditation, Yoga or Running club. [https://www.buchsys.de/paderborn/angebote/aktueller_zeitraum/index.html Further information and courses offered]
*'''Psychosocial counseling:''' Offer of counseling in confidential one-on-one conversation for students (also doctoral students). [https://zsb.uni-paderborn.de/psychosoziale-beratung/ Further information]
*'''Student Advice Centre:''' Various (online) offers for stress management (held in German), e.g. Autogenic training, "Overcoming fears and stress" or Forum "Psychologically fit studying." [https://zsb.uni-paderborn.de/angebote/veranstaltungskatalog/ Further information]

==Software Campus==
* [https://softwarecampus.de/ Software Campus]

==Volkshochschule Paderborn (VHS) - Adult Education Center==
*An adult education center ("Volkshochschule" (VHS)) is a non-profit institution for adult and continuing education. The Volkshochschule Paderborn offers courses and lectures in many different areas throughout the year: Languages, education, sport, handicrafts, photography, IT, fitness, nutrition, culture.... The courses offered by the VHS are subject to a fee, but are generally very affordable. A comprehensive catalog of all courses is published twice a year. [http://www.vhs-paderborn.de Further Information and Course Catalog]

title: Guide for meeting organization
wikitext:
==Guide for Meeting Organization==

===Get Prepared===
*Send out "Save the date" email
*Inform about accommodation options and how to get there 
*For bigger events:
**Set up registration tool (if needed for major events e.g. networks or schools), make sure to set it up so that participants receive a confirmation email after registration
**Prepare data protection consent form (if required)

===Obligatory Checks===
To avoid your expenses being rejected in an audit process, please check the following points beforehand:

*Check if the project has a budget for meeting expenses (e.g. ''AZA'')
*Get confirmation for budget from project manager
*Prepare participant list, hand it out and collect signatures from attendees for each day of the event
*Prepare agenda (with project logo and logo from granting authority if possible)
*Acknowledge granting authority in presentations (and agenda if possible)

===Think about parties to involve===
Mostly for bigger events, kickoffs or reviews only: 
*Granting Authority / Project Officer
*Press office (Pressestelle)
*Dissemination team of institute
*Dean (Dekan/Institutsleiter)

===Agenda===
*Prepare agenda structure
**Generally including partner presentations (if you meet for the first time) and WP presentations as well as project-specific presentations
**Circulate agenda among participants asap but at least by 2 weeks before (time limit often prescribed by Consortium Agreement and often needed well in advance by partners for travel applications).
*For plenaries:
**Prepare board meeting (official decision-making body of project → ask for partners’ input. Time limit often prescribed by Consortium Agreement.).
*For bigger events:
**You may want to have a higher-ranking person (e.g. dean, rector etc.) to give welcome speech. Make plans accordingly and as early as possible.

===Talks / Presentations===
*Organize project templates for slides (Are a project logo or corporate design available from dissemination team?)
*Discuss structure of WP presentation with consortium in monthly meetings before
*Provide space for uploading slides, demos etc.
*Specify who writes minutes and where (URL)

===Venue===
*Room booking (via the secretary’s office)
**Clarify whether you need additional rooms, e.g. for catering, storage, checkroom, parallel sessions ...
**Clarify if you need an application form to use the rooms/ lecture halls/ etc. (e.g. Zukunftsmeile 2).
*Depending on the location, prepare signposts or room plans to enable participants to find their way.

===Technical Needs===
*Appropriate equipment (for presentation in room (if needed, via IT unit))
**Equipment you might need: Beamer, laser pointer, extension cable...
*WIFI (ID/Pass) (via IT unit)
*For bigger events: 
**Under this [https://www.uni-paderborn.de/universitaet/presse-kommunikation-marketing/messe-ausstattung link] you can rent exhibition equipment, such as exhibition stands, roll-ups, brochure stands and beach flags of the UPB.
**Name badges (if needed, via secretary’s office)

===Food and Drinks===
*Catering for coffee breaks and lunch (via secretary’s office)
**Catering must be planned a couple of weeks before as Simone needs to get permission for expenses from UPB administration (via ''MACH'').
**Clarify whether it is necessary to obtain alternative offers
**Remember to provide alternatives for vegetarians/vegans and other diets 
**Catering providers in Paderborn: Studierendenwerk, Brand Manufaktur, Festfalen Catering...
**Make sure to have enough space and tables for the catering (Better to plan a few meters more!).
*Beverages for coffee breaks (via secretary’s office)
**Most catering providers offer drinks on consignment so that only the actual consumption has to be paid for.
*Dinner booking (via secretary’s office)

===Day of the Event===
* Get printouts of attendee list, agenda and data protection consent form (for guests)
* Place everything in meeting room
* Remind everyone to sign the attendee list

===Organising a Retreat===
# The first thing you need is a rough schedule and some information: How many days do you want the retreat/event to last? What is needed and what costs will be covered? Overnight stays? Meeting rooms? Meals? Approximately how many people will be attending? 
# Then it is best to get offers from different hotels and ask them for several periods. Make sure that the venue is easily accessible for all participants, preferably by car and public transport. Also make sure that the requested conference package includes everything you need (e.g. non-alcoholic drinks for the whole day). It is important for UPB's travel cost center (Dep. 4.1) to ensure that everything is included in the conference package because extra costs (e. g. for beverages) can't be charged.
# If you have comparative offers from the hotels, they must be submitted to the UPB Procurement Office ("Beschaffungsstelle", Dep. 1.4) (request through the Secretary's Office). Only when you get the okay from there, you can make the booking. It is also advisable to present the final offer of the hotel to a contact person of the travel cost center before booking, so that you can make sure that everything is in order with the offer and that all employees will be reimbursed in the end. In the meantime, you can check with the participants which of the possible dates for the retreat would be best, e.g. with a survey tool.
# Once you have the positive feedback from the procurement office and the travel cost center and a date for the retreat, you can make the booking with the hotel. After confirmation you can send a "Save the Date" to the participants.
# In the next step you can set up a registration form, clarify if you are allowed to use e.g. Google Forms or if this is not allowed - then there are also solutions from UPB. In both cases it is advisable to set it up so that participants receive a confirmation email after registration. Experience shows that many people forget whether they have already registered or not... Also consider whether certain information needs to be collected during registration, e.g. comments on food intolerances. Send an email with the link to register and set a deadline. About a week before the deadline you can send another reminder. Make sure that the registration period is long enough and does not necessarily fall in times when many people are on vacation.

===Organising an Advisory Board Meeting (online)===
* Focus on technical/scientific WPs (Keep them brief. Only if there is time, present Dissemination & Exploitation topics or other.)  
* Structure of presentations (2-3 slides per task/ research topic/ etzc.)  
** Main question/ goal
** Publications/ project outputs
** Highlights achieved
* Provide AB members with a list of the most important publications

title: HPC-PC2
wikitext: This page gives some hints how to use the High Performance Cluster PC2 within the DICE Group. Currently the OCuLUS cluster is most relevant for us since it is the only cluster that provides GPU support. == Getting Access == Ask your group lead to get access. == Accessing The Cluster == See https://uni-paderborn.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PC2DOK/pages/12944205/Access+and+Login == Conda Environment == * Load Anaconda ** module load lang ** module load Anaconda3 * Change the global defaults of conda (the group might be hpc-prf-diceml) ** conda config --add envs_dirs /scratch///.conda/envs ** conda config --add pkgs_dirs /scratch///.conda/pkgs * Run conda init * Install dependencies (e.g., via a environmenty.yml or requirements.txt file) * Starting a job ** Start an interactive job with srun -t 30:00 -p gpu --mem 20g python program.py ** Start a batch job with sbatch job-noctua2.sh with the file [https://github.com/dice-group/HPC-PC2/blob/main/job-noctua2.sh job-noctua2.sh] == Troubleshooting == * Start an interactive job with srun -t 30:00 --gres=gpu:a100:1 --pty bash == Accessing The Cluster [OCuLUS, deprecated] == * Log in to one of the frontend servers of OCuLUS via ssh ** ssh @fe.pc2.uni-paderborn.de ** ssh @fe-2.cv2012.pc2.uni-paderborn.de * Setup configuration files of the Job Manager CCS (only once if you are new to the OCULUS cluster) ** Execute ccsgenrcfiles (see [https://wikis.uni-paderborn.de/pc2doc/OpenCCSFaQ#How_to_set_up_the_CCS_configuration_file.3F How to set up the CCS configuration file?]) You need to use the [[VPN]] or tunnel via an sshgate ([[Remote_Access#SSH_tunnel_into_UPB]]). For further details, see https://wikis.uni-paderborn.de/pc2doc/OCuLUS You have two ways how to install Python packages and dependencies on the cluster: Conda and Singularity. Package managers like apt do not work on the PC2 since you do not have root access. == Conda Environment + ccsalloc [OCuLUS, deprecated] == * Creating an environment ** Option 1: Download and install conda following [https://docs.conda.io/projects/conda/en/latest/user-guide/install/linux.html Manual] *** wget https://repo.anaconda.com/miniconda/Miniconda3-latest-Linux-x86_64.sh *** bash Miniconda3-latest-Linux-x86_64.sh *** Choose the path $PC2PFS///miniconda3 during installation *** To accelerate the file-I/O and avoid quota problems with $HOME, you may establish softlinks from $HOME/.local and $HOME/.cache to your $PC2PFS group directory[https://wikis.uni-paderborn.de/pc2doc/OCuLUS-FAQ#Install_Python_packages_.28in_your_home_directory.29] ** Option 2: Use anaconda module by PC2: [[Creating Conda Env. on PC2 OCuLUS]] (seems to be broken) ** Option 3: Create pip environment: [https://wikis.uni-paderborn.de/pc2doc/OCuLUS-FAQ#Install_Python_packages_.28in_your_home_directory.29 PC2: How to Install Python Packages (in your Home Directory)] * Starting a Job **ccsalloc -I -s now --duration 2h --res=rset=1:ncpus=8:mem=20g:gpus=1:rtx2080=t python .py *** ncpus specifies the number of cpus and can be changed *** rtx2080=t specifies the GPU and can also be replaced with gtx1080=t *** -I specifies *interactive* mode which allows to see the output of the job in the terminal. The job can be stopped with Ctrl-C. * Tips ** If your code needs to store the results at the end, make sure you are on a writable file system. E.g., you can create a repository in scratch: cd $PC2PFS/hpc-prf-diceml, then mkdir -p /. You can then put your code in and run it with PC2 gpus :) ** To download the results from the server, use the following on a terminal of your local machine: scp -i /.ssh/authorized_keys username@fe.pc2.uni-paderborn.de://scratch/hpc-prf-diceml/username/Foldername/resultsfile.txt ./ . You will be asked to authenticate, use the same password as the one you used to login. Once you enter your password, the file will be downloaded in the local repository where your terminal was open. ** Further information about running jobs can be obtained with ccsinfo -s --mine followed by ccsinfo ** You can also run Jupyterlab from the conda/pip environement: *** Start Jupyter Lab in Interactive Session: ccsalloc -I -s now --duration 2h --res=rset=1:ncpus=8:mem=20g:gpus=1:rtx2080=t jupyter lab --ip 0.0.0.0 --port 8888 *** Create a new shell to forward port: ssh @fe-2.cv2012.pc2.uni-paderborn.de: -L 8888::8888 (The nodename can be seen in the output of the previous ccsalloc/jupyter command.) *** Open Jupyter in your own browser: http://localhost:8888/ == Singularity Container + jupyterspawner == * Jupyter with Tensorflow and GPU Support ** module load jupyterspawner ** jupyterspawner --start --gpu gtx1080=1 --ncpus 16 --singularity $PC2SW/SINGULARITY/Images/TENSORFLOW/TENSORFLOW_2.7.0_CUDA11.2_PYTHON3.sif * Jupyter with PyTorch and GPU Support ** Singularity Recipe for PyTorch on GPU in Jupyter: [https://github.com/dice-group/HPC-PC2/blob/main/pytorch-gpu.def pytorch-gpu.def] (works for GTX 1080 and RTX 2080, not tesla) ** Build singularity image on local machine: singularity build pytorch-gpu.sif pytorch-gpu.def ** Copy image to PC2: scp pytorch-gpu.sif @fe-2.cv2012.pc2.uni-paderborn.de:/upb/departments/pc2/groups/hpc-prf-diceml//singularity/pytorch-gpu.sif ** module load jupyterspawner ** jupyterspawner --start --gpu gtx1080=1 --ncpus 16 --singularity $PC2DATA/hpc-prf-diceml//singularity/pytorch-gpu.sif ** See [https://wikis.uni-paderborn.de/pc2doc/Jupyter PC² wiki: Jupyter] for further information * Create Own Singularity Container ** See [https://wikis.uni-paderborn.de/pc2doc/JupyterHub#Create_my_own_singularity_container Create Own Singularity Container] ** Keep in mind that the version numbers must be compatible (e.g., [https://developer.nvidia.com/cuda-gpus CUDA compute capability], pytorch/tensorflow [pre-]compiled for the CUDA compute capabilities) ** Helpful commands to check compatibility might be the command line tools nvcc --version and nvidia-smi, and the Python commands torch.version.cuda and torch.cuda.get_arch_list() ** Please add your own containers to our GitHub repository so that others can build upon it: https://github.com/dice-group/HPC-PC2/ == Acknowledgement Statement for Publications == All publications, where the use of PC² computing resources was instrumental, must include the following acknowledgement: {| class="wikitable" |- | The authors gratefully acknowledge the funding of this project by computing time provided by the Paderborn Center for Parallel Computing (PC²). |} In LaTeX you can use the command PC\textsuperscript{2}. In case there are formatting problems with "PC²" you can also write "PC2" instead. See: https://pc2.uni-paderborn.de/de/hpc-services/our-services/forms-documents/acknowledgement == PC² HPC Introduction Courses == * [https://pc2.uni-paderborn.de/teaching/trainings/hpc-user-trainings/old/linux-introduction-course/material Course Material: Linux Introduction Course from PC²] * [https://pc2.uni-paderborn.de/teaching/trainings/hpc-user-trainings/old/hpc-introduction-course/material Course Material: HPC Introduction Course from PC²] * [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1M4wvDYpc3Ui2QPP8jN6xpbUhQvz98I3TqtptaWxKo34/ Notes from 2022-02-01] == Further information == * PC2: https://wikis.uni-paderborn.de/pc2doc/Hauptseite ** PC2 doc: https://uni-paderborn.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PC2DOK/overview ** [https://pc2.uni-paderborn.de/teaching/trainings/hpc-user-trainings HPC User Training] ** [https://events.uni-paderborn.de/category/13/ HPC Consultation Hour] * OCuLUS: https://wikis.uni-paderborn.de/pc2doc/OCuLUS * PC2 Scripts by DICE Group: [https://github.com/dice-group/HPC-PC2 GitHub DICE repository HPC-PC2] * External: https://researchcomputing.princeton.edu/support/knowledge-base/jupyter

Hiring students
wikitext:
=== General === * Students can be hired as SHK (no university degree), WHB (with a Bachelor's degree) or WHK (with a Master's degree) depending on the degree they have. * Students from other universities can also be hired. It requires an informal written statement confirming that no student from UPB fits the position or is available. Give reasons why. The statement must be submitted as part of the contract application. === Advertise the job === ==== Website and online form ==== * Our open student positions are listed here: [https://dice-research.org/jobs#student-assistant-positions dice-research.org/jobs#student-assistant-positions]. * To add a new job position: ** Use the GitHub website directory [https://github.com/dice-group/dice-website/tree/develop/pages/jobs /pages/jobs] to create a description for the job. There is also a template file. ** Add your new created site at the list of open student assistant jobs ([https://github.com/dice-group/dice-website/blob/develop/pages/jobs.mdx /pages/jobs.mdx]). * The applications are handeled by an online form (admin: Nikit).
Results are automatically send to the mailinglist dice-jobs@lists.uni-paderborn.de ([https://lists.uni-paderborn.de/mailman/listinfo/dice-jobs info], [https://lists.uni-paderborn.de/mailman/private/dice-jobs/ archive], [https://lists.uni-paderborn.de/mailman/simple/dice-jobs admin], [https://lists.uni-paderborn.de/mailman/admin/dice-jobs admin expert], admins: Adrian, Micha) ==== Mailinglists ==== Send a mail to one or several of the follow mailing lists: * studierende-informatik@lists.uni-paderborn.de ** All CS students will receive a mail ** In the past, they did not accept job offer mails for some time ** all WINFO students are included. There should be no need to add jobs@fsrwinfo.de and fsrwinfo@lists.uni-paderborn.de * jobs-eim@upb.de ** Probably there is only a couple of students who receive mails there * studierende-computerengineering@lists.uni-paderborn.de * jobs@fsrwinfo.de * infosfuerstudierende@lists.uni-paderborn.de Your mail could look about like this: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1NuNJmdaZfqYic8wVfUT2vs5rD9XWxYttuwOIPBZEiVI/edit?usp=sharing ==== Twitter / LinkedIn / AStA ==== * We can also use Twitter. Ask Franzi. * We can use our LinkedIn account ([https://www.linkedin.com/company/dice-research/ linkedin.com/company/dice-research/]) to post jobs. Ask Franzi. * Post it to the "jobbörse" of the AStA (student council): https://asta.uni-paderborn.de/jobboerse/ === Test the student === Depending on the tasks for the student, we already have several tests which should show whether the student is able to work for the group or not. Several tests are available in the [https://svn.dice-research.org/closed/organization/job_tests/ SVN]. For programming tests, ask Micha. === Hire a student=== ==== Negotiate contract details ==== * Type of position ** Depending on the available degree of the student ** SHK (without a university degree), WHB (with a Bachelor's degree), WHK (with a Master's degree) * WHK - special contract type ** Counted toward the maximum fixed-term employment period acc. to the Wissenschaftszeitvertragsgesetz / German Academic Fixed-Term Contract Act ([https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/wisszeitvg/ WissZeitVG]) ** Minimum of 10 hours/week required (acc. to UPB's HR office) and up to 19 hours/week possible ** Publication of job ad required or approval from all councils to waive job ad (justification required) ** Job description: '''no research''' tasks, '''only support''' tasks ** TV-L contract as a researcher prefered to WHK employment (Academic staff council will ask for your reasons to hire a WHK and not a junior researcher.) ** Change from WHB to WHK: WHB contract will be terminated. A new contract for WHK will be concluded. Due to the new hire as a WHK, publication of job ad and a job description are required and hence more time is needed. Don't terminate WHB contract before WHK contract is ready for signature. * Duration ** Contracts '''must be offered''' for a year (based on [https://www.tdl-online.de/fileadmin/user_upload/231209_Einigungspapier_v._9.12.2023_-_finale_Fassung.pdf TV-L amendment] from 9 December 2023). ** Shorter contract periods can be requested by the student for personal reasons or stating other reasons (e.g. end of studies, expiry of visa, etc.) in the application forms (for [https://www.uni-paderborn.de/fileadmin/zv/4-3/WHB/Anlage_zum_WHB_Antrag_Stand_25.03.2024.pdf WHB], for [https://www.uni-paderborn.de/fileadmin/zv/4-3/SHK/Anlage_zum_SHK-Antrag_Stand_25.03.2024.pdf SHK]). ** Shorter contracts can exceptionally be issued by us if clear and verifiable reasons are available (i.e. options limited to tutoring and similar cases). Reasons must also be given in the application forms (for [https://www.uni-paderborn.de/fileadmin/zv/4-3/WHB/Anlage_zum_WHB_Antrag_Stand_25.03.2024.pdf WHB], for [https://www.uni-paderborn.de/fileadmin/zv/4-3/SHK/Anlage_zum_SHK-Antrag_Stand_25.03.2024.pdf SHK]). {| class="wikitable" |- | '''Example for a six-month tutor contract:''' Anzukreuzen ist der Punkt "Befristete Aufgaben". Laut Frau Meier-Rohde reichen 1-2 Sätze mit etwa folgendem Inhalt. "Es handelt sich um ein Tutorium, das inklusive Vor- und Nachbereitung 6 Monate lang dauert." |} * Reduction/ Termination of contracts ** Justifications for contracts less than 12 months must be short and concise. Remember the fewer the words, the fewer questions there are from the "authorities". ** Justifications for contracts less than 12 months provided for WHBs and WHKs are reviewed by the academic staff council who will do random checks among the students and inquire about the reasons given. ** A first-time 12-month contract includes a trial period of 4 months in which the contract can be terminated with a two-week notice (i.e. add time for internal processes at DICE and HR service). A termination of contract requires a legally valid justification that can be substantiated by you (through emails, notes, measurable results, etc.). Please be prepared as supervisors for such a situation. * Weekly hours ** 19 working hours per week (including all job engagements of the student) are maximum work load for a student and regarded as full-time employments. ** If the student works less hours (i.e. part-time), there is a minijob ceiling that the student may not want to cross. (Minijob means that the student will pay less social security contribution and receive more net salary per hour. This may also be relevant for BAföG payments.) ** See table below and check with your student whether a 'minijob' is preferred. {| class="wikitable" |+ Minijob ceiling |- ! Position !! from 01/01/2025 !! from 01/04/2025 |- | SHK (see [https://www.uni-paderborn.de/zv/4-3/shk employer cost table]) || up to 9.5 hrs/w || up to 8.5 hrs/w |- | WHB (see [https://www.uni-paderborn.de/zv/4-3/beschaeftigung-von-whb employer cost table]) || up to 8 hrs/w || up to 8 hrs/w |- | WHK (see [https://www.uni-paderborn.de/zv/4-2/wissenschaftliche-hilfskraefte/informationen-fuer-fakultaeten employer cost table]) || up to 6 hrs/w || up to 6 hrs/w |} ==== Apply for a contract or contract renewal ==== *Supervisors clarify contract details with student *Supervisors clarify available budget (which requires information about contract duration, weekly hours, present degree) with Nadine. She can also provide the correct billing object number (Abrechnungsobjekt, AO). * Supervisors inform students to get contract as agreed (i.e. contract period, weekly hours, paying project) by filling out all forms (see next bullet point) as required and submitting them in printing to Simone. * Forms under #1 on the following pages have to be filled for a first-time contract. Forms under #3 have to be filled for a contract renewal. ** SHK: https://www.uni-paderborn.de/zv/4-3/shk/ ** WHB: https://www.uni-paderborn.de/zv/4-3/beschaeftigung-von-whb/ ** WHK: We have to use the official UPB workflow. Please ask Simone for details. * Simone will process the documents submitted by the student and send them to the HR department. * Time needed before a contract is issued/ renewed (not including the time you need for clarifying the job details with your student): ** for SHK: '''4 weeks''' (needed by HR) '''+ 2 weeks''' (needed to get signatures from Axel and the CS institute plus the internal UPB mail delivery) ** for WHB/WHK: '''6 weeks''' (needed by HR) '''+ 2 weeks''' (needed to get signatures from Axel and the CS institute plus the internal UPB mail delivery) ** FYI: WHB/WHK employment require approval by the academic staff council and hence take more time (i.e. 6 weeks).

title: Illness
wikitext:
== Illness and work ==

There are several, important rules that you have to follow in case of getting ill. The rules are listed below. 

=== 1st day of illness===

* '''MUST''': In the case of sick leave, open [https://zeiterfassung.uni-paderborn.de/ ATOSS] (only accessible via the university network or via VPN). Report "Sick note without AU". 
* ''Note that missing this could lead to severe drawbacks in case of a severe disease!''
* Please add your absence to the "DICE group office absence" '''calendar'''.
* Important note: The obligation to notify also applies if you are unable to work abroad or on vacation. In order to be able to credit vacation time, you must always provide proof of illness in the form of a medical certificate from the very first day.

see also: https://www.uni-paderborn.de/fileadmin/zv/4-3/Urlaub/Krankmeldungen/Schaubild_Krankmeldungen_03.07.2024.pdf

=== 3nd/4th day of illness ===

* '''MUST''': If your illness lasts longer than 3 calendar days, a doctor has to confirm the illness.

*Case 1 (you have statutory health insurance, e.g. Techniker Krankenkasse, Barmer etc.): Doctor writes an electronic certificate of incapacity for work (eAU = "Elektronische Arbeitsunfähigkeitsbescheinigung"). Report "First sick note with eAU" in [https://zeiterfassung.uni-paderborn.de/ ATOSS]. This authorises the employer to request the medically vertified darta on incapacity for work from the health insurance fund. Then inform Axel about the expected duration of the illness. 
* Case 2 (you are at a private health insurance (NOT the case for the majority e.g. at Techniker Krankenkasse): a certificate of incapacity ("AU", [https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arbeitsunf%C3%A4higkeitsbescheinigung#Formular Wikipedia: Arbeitsunfähigkeitsbescheinigung]) for work from the doctor has to be required. It comprises 3 pages: One page should be sent to your health insurance ("Krankenversicherung"). One page is for your files, you should keep it. There is a page named "Ausfertigung zur Vorlage beim Arbeitgeber". Report "First sick note with paper sick note" in [https://zeiterfassung.uni-paderborn.de/ ATOSS] and send the "Ausfertigung zur Vorlage beim Arbeitgeber" by post or digitally to the HR department. 
** If you have a contract at the UPB, you have to send it to the address listed below.
** If you have a contract with another university (e.g., Leipzig) it has to be sent to this university.
** If you receive a stipend, you do not have to send it.

  Address for "AU":
  Universität Paderborn
  Dezernat 4.3
  Warburger Str. 100
  33098 Paderborn

=== Being sick over the weekend ===

When does the sick note have to be submitted to the employer if you feel a bit unwell on Friday and stay at home, but are still ill on Monday? If the weekend is between two sick days, it counts towards the three-day period - because it's about calendar days, not working days. This means that if you stay home sick from Friday and are still unfit for work on Monday, the certificate must be submitted to your employer on Monday - even if Saturday and Sunday are days off for you. However, if your doctor's only sends the eAU to the health insurance fund in the afternoon or evening on Monday, your employer may not be able to retrieve it until Tuesday. If you have private health insurance, you are also still obliged to send the sick note to your employer yourself. This can quickly become stressful. It is therefore better to go to the doctor immediately on Friday if you suspect that you might not be fit again on Monday (Source [https://www.advocard.de/streitlotse/arbeit-und-karriere/krankmeldung-alles-was-du-wissen-musst/ Advocard])

=== Extension of illness ===
If your illness lasts longer than expected you need to immediately, please consult your doctor again and update the information via the ''sick note form'' (and AU, if private insurance) as described above. ''Note that missing this could lead to severe drawbacks in case of a severe disease!''

=== 1st day back at work ===
* '''MUST''': please '''report healthy''' by report "Health notification" in [https://zeiterfassung.uni-paderborn.de/ ATOSS].

=== Sick leave for Student Assitants ===
In the case of sick leave you need a formal notification to the HR department which must include: 1. start of the incapacity to work and 2. expected end of the illness. Send the notification to '''krankmeldungen-hk@zv.upb.de'''  and also inform your supervisor. See this overview for the whole process: https://www.uni-paderborn.de/fileadmin/zv/4-3/Urlaub/Krankmeldungen/Schaubild_Krankmeldungen_03.07.2024.pdf

On your first day back at work please '''report healthy''' by sending a mail to '''krankmeldungen-hk@zv.upb.de''' with '''[https://dice-research.org/SimoneAuinger Simone]''' in CC.

=== Sources ===
* [https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/entgfg/__5.html EFZG §5] ''Dauert die Arbeitsunfähigkeit länger als drei Kalendertage, hat der Arbeitnehmer eine ärztliche Bescheinigung über das Bestehen der Arbeitsunfähigkeit sowie deren voraussichtliche Dauer spätestens an dem darauffolgenden Arbeitstag vorzulegen.''
* UPB info pages: [https://www.uni-paderborn.de/en/zv/4-2/research-assistants/translate-to-english-informationen-fuer-whk/translate-to-english-arbeitsunfaehigkeit Incapacity to work] and [https://www.uni-paderborn.de/zv/4-2/wissenschaftliche-hilfskraefte/informationen-fuer-whk/arbeitsunfaehigkeit Arbeitsunfaehigkeit]
* [https://www.uni-paderborn.de/fileadmin/zv/4-3/Urlaub/Krankmeldungen/Schaubild_Krankmeldungen_03.07.2024.pdf Overview figure]

== How to find medical help in Germany ==

You should:
* have a family doctor,
* have a dentist,
* have a [https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elektronische_Gesundheitskarte health insurance card],
* be aware of the nearest pharmacies.

In case you do not feel well and you need help you should contact your family doctor. He will do a diagnosis and decide what to do. In case of problems with your teeth, you should go directly to your dentist. For all other specialist, you first need to go to your family doctor since he has to forward you. Typically, it is sufficient to call the doctor and ask for an appointment. If you feel pain, you need to mention that to ensure that you get an earlier appointment. In this case, you may even directly go to the doctor during his consultation-hours.

'''In all cases (even emergencies) you have to take your health insurance card with you!'''

However, there are situations, in which you can not wait for the next consultation-hour of your family doctor. Here, we can mainly differentiate between the following two cases.

Case 1: Emergency! Your life (or the life of a relative) is in danger (e.g., serious blood loss, heart attack, severe accident, broken bones, etc.):
* Dial `112`. You should mention your name, your location and the problem that you have. An ambulance will come and pick you up.
* You can also go to the hospital by yourself. However, if you can still go there by yourself, you should ask yourself whether it is really an emergency ;)

Case 2: It is not an emergency (i.e., it is not a life-threatening situation). However, you need treatment fast and your family doctor (or dentist) is not available. It may also be possible that you just need a certain drug, but the pharmacies are already closed. At nearly all times, there are some doctors, dentists and pharmacies available for this kind of situation. Depending on whom you need, you may proceed in a different way:
* Doctor
** The Medico has special service hours and is located near the University (https://www.notdienst-paderborn.de/). Please note that the Medico is the building in front of the hospital; it is not part of the hospital.
** You can use the search at https://www.116117.de/bps/web/index.php/de/search
** Dial `116 117`. You should mention your name, your location and the problem that you have. 
* Dentist
** You can use the search at https://www.zahnaerzte-wl.de/ (Press "Patient & Notdienst" on top and choose your city) or go to [https://www.zahnaerzte-wl.de/pages/notdienstsuche] to get available Dentists in Westfalen-Lippe
** Dial `01805/986 700`. You should mention your name, your location and the problem that you have. (taken from [https://www.praxisnetz-pb.de/fuer-patienten/notdienst/])
* Pharmacy
** You can use the search at https://www.aponet.de/apotheke/notdienstsuche

wikitext:
== Proposal Phase ==

If you want to write a proposal in Latex, you can invite non-UPB collaborators via a UPB guest account to join your UPB Overleaf project.

=== Workflow ===

# Create guest accounts for all collaborators in the ZIM self-service portal (see https://hilfe.uni-paderborn.de/Erstellung_eines_Uni-Accounts_(Gaeste))
# Collaborators must go through the registration process. They have to ensure that they finish the process!
# Collaborators must enable overleaf in the self-service portal (see https://hilfe.uni-paderborn.de/Overleaf)
# Collaborators may have to login to the UPB overleaf at least once (Should be double checked!)
# You can share the proposal via the UPB e-mail address of the guest accounts

=== Text Snippets ===

The following text describes the actions that should be done by the invited collaborator to get a guest account:

 You should have received a mail from "IMT Benutzerberatung" with a link that enables you to create your account. While the mail is in German and English, the linked page is only available in German.
 On the linked page, you should simply press the button "Uni-Account erstellen" to create your account. The account creation comprises 7 pages. You can navigate between them with the "Weiter" and "Zurück" buttons which mean forward and backward, respectively.
 
 1/7: The first page should already contain your basic information. Please check the fields and set your birth date. If the page is shown in German, the fields have the following meaning:
 Vorname = first name 
 Nachname = last name 
 Akademischer Titel = academic title 
 Geschlecht = gender 
 Geburtsdatum = birth date
 2/7: This page is about your contact details. Your email should already be listed and the options say that all messages that you should get to your guest account will be forwarded to your mail address. You can also add a phone number, but that is optional.
 3/7: On this page, you can choose your user name. There are some suggestions but you can also choose a different name (as long as it has not been taken by another user).
 4/7: This page asks you to set your password and repeat it in the second box. Note that the password has to fulfill the following criteria:
    • It needs to have at least 8 characters and contain at least
    • 1 digit character
    • 1 special character
    • 1 capital letter
 5/7: This page lists the services the university offers based on your account. You can simply leave the configuration as it is.
 6/7: This page lists the legal rules for the account. At the top, you can find a link to download them as PDF.
 7/7: This page summarizes your entered data. You can finish the account creation with the "Uni-Account jetzt mit diesen Daten erzeugen" button.

== Running Project ==

*'''Document management''': SVN (not Git, as single work packages). Must contain a public part for publication PDFs. Deliverables and all versioned documents live here.
** Naming convention: https://svn.dice-research.org/lowercase-project-name
*'''Joint editing''': Cryptpad, Etherpad. All joint editing is to be carried out here. Todos are to be linked to the calendar. Should provide wiki-like functionality. Must be versioned.
*'''Code''': GitHub/GitLab. Prefer GitHub.
*'''Calendar''': Add all appointments and all reminders in here. Automatic mails to mailing list.
*'''Publication management''': Bibsononmy, PDF in public part of SVN. Important control point for the management. Publications submitted to the EU must be available here including PDFs in SVN (see above).
*'''Mailing lists''': 1 general mailing list (mailman, Paderborn university). Management and research mailing lists can be considered if the project is large. Regarded as not necessary for smaller projects (<10 partners). Work packages can create own mailing lists if wanted. All calender reminders go to general mailing list.
*'''Polls''': Choose alternatives that are GDPR-conform, have no ads and can be displayed in English. An open-source service we used before is https://bitpoll.mafiasi.de/. Find out more about available options in this [https://www.der-paritaetische.de/themen/bereichsuebergreifende-themen/gleichimnetz/webzeugkoffer/faq/doodle-dudle-foodle-co-was-ist-das-beste-tool-zur-terminfindung/ article] from 2020 [or add newer sources if you've come across any].
*'''Project corporate design''': A logo is usually provided for each project. Granting auhtorities also tend to like project consortiums to have common presentation templates for a project. See if you or a partner can take care of it.

title: LGDSetup
wikitext: == Internal LinkedGeoData Setup == LinkedGeoData for whole Germany is provided using Virtuoso with data generated from Open Street Map (OSM) files taken from [http://download.geofabrik.de/europe/germany.html]. Generating LinkedGeoData from OSM files is described here [[Medium:LGD_setup.pdf]]. === Starting docker container (the new method is necessary to have the geoSPARQL extensions feature by making use of another docker image) === Run the following command: sudo docker run -d --rm --name lgd_de19 -e DBA_PASSWORD=XXX -it -v /data/lgd/vos19/database:/database -v /data/lgd/bnds:/rdfGer -t -p 1111:1111 -p 8890:8890 -i openlink/virtuoso-opensource-7 === Building docker image === To build the docker image from Dockerfile, the following commands were used: sudo wget http://vos.openlinksw.com/owiki/wiki/VOS/VirtuosoDocker/Dockerfile.vos_base ## NB:start in an empty folder sudo docker build -f Dockerfile.vos_base -t openlink/vos_base:v0 . sudo wget http://vos.openlinksw.com/owiki/wiki/VOS/VirtuosoDocker/Dockerfile.vos sudo docker build -f Dockerfile.vos -t openlink/vos:v0 . === Start a VOS container === Run the following commands: sudo mkdir -p /opt/virtuoso-opensource/var/lib/virtuoso/db sudo wget http://vos.openlinksw.com/owiki/wiki/VOS/VirtuosoDocker/virtuoso.ini.template sudo cp ./virtuoso.ini.template /opt/virtuoso-opensource/var/lib/virtuoso/db/virtuoso.ini sudo docker run --name lgd-virtuoso -d --restart always -v /data/virtuoso-opensource/var/lib/virtuoso/db:/opt/virtuoso-opensource/var/lib/virtuoso/db -v /data/lgd/bnds:/rdfGer -p 1111:1111 -p 8890:8890 -i openlink/vos:v0 === Loading data to the instance === Check if there is already data at /data/virtuoso-opensource/var/lib/virtuoso/db. '''If yes, skip this step!''' isql tool was used to load triples from .nt files (15 files). sudo docker exec -it trusting_shaw /bin/bash cd /opt/virtuoso-opensource/bin sudo ./isql 1111 For example the following SQL script loads data for saarland: delete from DB.DBA.LOAD_LIST; commit work; ld_add('/rdfGer/saarland.nt','lgd'); rdf_loader_run (); checkpoint;

= Available deployments = == UPB == === UPB LLM chat === https://ai-chat.upb.de/ (needs activation in ZIM Serviceportal, see https://hilfe.uni-paderborn.de/AI-Chat) Take a note of where is each model hosted. With some of them the data might be sent to other companies for processing.
Diese technische Gestaltung gewährleistet, dass keine Anmeldedaten wie Benutzernamen oder andere persönliche Informationen weitergegeben werden. Lediglich die Eingaben, also die Prompts, werden über die API-Schnittstelle an den externen Dienst übermittelt. https://hilfe.uni-paderborn.de/Datenschutz_bei_KI-Diensten
=== UPB LLM API === https://ai-gateway.upb.de/ (needs e-mail request, see https://hilfe.uni-paderborn.de/AI-Gateway) == DICE == === Support === '''For all questions related to DICE LLM resources please contact only via {{Matrix link|#dice-llm-chat:chat.dice-research.org}}.''' If you would like to request a specific model, please check if it is supported by [https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/models/supported_models/ vLLM] and can be deployed on a single H100 with 80 gigabytes of memory, write a message with the details. === DICE LLM chat === https://dice-llm-chat.cs.uni-paderborn.de/ Sign in using your IRB Gitlab account. If your account requires activation, write a message with the details in the channel mentioned above. This is our internal, standalone service, which is currently unrelated to UPB's LLM service or any company. We use our own computing resources to deploy open-source models. We also offer services such as image generation and voice chat. This calls our own API behind the scenes, see below. === DICE LLM API === We try to provide a set of currently relevant models available as an API for the purposes of IDE integration, local development, testing, experiments (where runtime is not important) and demos. We provide some models: - some on an always loaded and ready basis; there are also aliases general-purpose and agentic-coding provided for seamless migration when new version appear, these two name will always point to our new model that provides reliable service - recommended to use if you don't require exact specific version of some model, for the best experience; - Experimental models offer people more choices, but to save GPUs, they do not remain permanently on the GPU. So they are models on-demand basis; a first query might take some time (minutes), so in some cases you might want to first run a warm-up query: Click here for information on the models we currently support: https://dice-llm-api.cs.uni-paderborn.de/ "warm" usually means these models are always resident on the GPU, "cold" usually means they are those "experimental models", they must be loaded from the hard drive. They only be loaded when a request was recieved. This may result in a wait of several minutes before you receive a response, and the models will be unloaded from the GPU after 10 minutes of inactivity. ==== Requesting access ==== To get an access token, '''write a message in the channel mentioned above''' with the following details: 
Who will use it: (IMT username - can be you or a student)
Light or heavy usage, with short description: (...)
Which project (if applicable):
Do not delete your message afterwards. ==== Usage policy ==== ===== For light usage ===== * For connecting to IDEs, general purpose chat, coding tasks etc. * Only the most common models are available (general-purpose and agentic-coding). * Access token is issued for 90 days (30 days for students). Afterwards you can ask for an extension or for a new access token. ===== For heavy usage ===== * For running experiments. * More models are available on demand. * Access token is issued for 15 days (also for students). Afterwards you can ask for an extension or for a new access token. * We might limit the amount of heavyweight access tokens issued simultaneously to avoid performance degradation. ===== For demos ===== TODO ==== Usage ==== URL: https://dice-llm-api.cs.uni-paderborn.de/v1 List the available models: 
curl --location 'https://dice-llm-api.cs.uni-paderborn.de/v1/models' --header 'Authorization: Bearer '
And then query any of the models by using our generic alias or their specific ID like this: 
curl --location 'https://dice-llm-api.cs.uni-paderborn.de/v1/chat/completions' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer ' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data '{
      "model": "general-purpose",
      "messages": [
        {
          "role": "user",
          "content": "Why is sky blue?"
        }
      ]
}'
==== Inference Parameters ==== Here's how you can use inference parameters: For example, here is how you can control temperature, top_k, top_p and whether inference is enabled. This will be very helpful for your experiment. 
curl -sS --request POST  'https://dice-llm-api.cs.uni-paderborn.de/v1/chat/completions' \
    --header 'Authorization: Bearer ' \
    --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    --data '{
    "model": "qwen3.8-27b-fp8",
    "messages": [
      {
        "role": "user",
        "content": "Choose one random English word from: apple, banana, cherry, orange, grape. Reply with only that word."
      }
    ],
    "max_tokens": 32,
    "temperature": 1.0,
    "top_p": 1.0,
    "top_k": 1,
    "stream": false,
    "chat_template_kwargs": {
      "enable_thinking": false
    }
    }' | jq
However, please note that not all models have enable_thinking as their inference switch. For specific models, you may need to find the corresponding switch. Some models may not be able to shut down inference completely, due to it does not provide by itself. ==== Troubleshooting ==== 
# TODO
TOKEN=
MODEL=general-purpose
time curl ... $TOKEN # warm-up query
time curl ... $TOKEN # real query
The list of currently available models (in addition to the recommended aliases): https://dice-llm-api.cs.uni-paderborn.de/ === Management === {| class="wikitable" ! URL !! Credentials |- | https://dice-llm-api.cs.uni-paderborn.de/ui/ || [[Vault]] |}
