title: Leaving Germany to live in another EU country
wikitext:
== Disclaimer == 
* This article provides information based on a personal experience, moving from Germany to the UK (December 2018, pre-Brexit), as an EU citizen (not German); so in case of visa requirements/changes, please check with the local Ausländerbehörde. 
* Additionally, the main author of this article had a contract with URZ (Universität Leipzig), so some of the following steps might or might not apply to you''

== Most Important Step ==

Most agencies require '''a three months -at least- written notice''' to terminate your contract. 

'''Your preferable termination date must be at least 3 months from the day you send the letter.'''
''For example, if you send your letter at 15th August 2019 to e.g. the electricity company, the first available date to ask for termination will be 16th November 2019.'' 
Additionally, you need to check your contract regarding the delay between the letter and the ending of the contract. There are cases that the termination can take place at the end of requested month ''e.g. November 2019, and not the 16th''. In case you receive a termination date that violates your contract, send them a letter back mentioning the contract. Otherwise, you will have to comply. You can try to ask for an earlier than 3 months termination, but your chances of success a low to non-existent. 

A termination letter must include:
* The reason you want to terminate your contract. Make it clear that you are moving out of Germany and not in another part of Germany.
* The date you want your contract to be terminated.  
* The date you are leaving Germany.
* Your name, fully written.
* Your signature.
* Your email address. Use a personal email address because the university one might size to exist after some months.
 
It can also include, though not obligatory:
* A corresponding address they can reach you after you move from Germany. It can be either:
** your new place of living
** a family member or a friend's address that is valid 
* Your phone number, but mention until when it will be valid.


Once you write the termination letter, most agencies will write you back asking for proof that you are leaving Germany and/or proof that you are moving to a new country.
The most valid proof to show that you are leaving Germany is to send them a copy from your unregistration from the Bürgeramt. For reasons explained below, you will be able to receive this proof only within the last 7 days before your departure. Do not get anxious, you can send the copy of the unregistration once you have it.


In case you want to sell things, [https://www.ebay-kleinanzeigen.de/ Ebay's Kleinanzeigen] is a very helpful website. Please take all necessary precautions that you would normally take when you give personal information on the internet. Only available in German, but it is pretty easy to understand how it works.

== House agency ==
''Note: this information applies when you rent a property and you are the only tenant. In case you live in students dorms or share a flat with other people, you might need to take other and/or extra steps.

* Write them a letter 3 months in advance and tell them you are leaving. In most cases they need a notice 3 months before you leave. Read your contract to be sure about it. In my case, I sent a letter around 24th September but the date I could to officially leave the flat was then 31st December. Also, I mentioned to my letter that I will be leaving the country on the 7th December, even though I could have stayed until the 31st. Even in that case, I had to pay the whole rent for December 2018. You can try persuading them not to pay the whole month if you want to leave earlier but in most cases they will not accept.
* Set a date before you leave so someone from the agency will come for the final investigation of the house i.e. someone checks the status of the house before you give the keys. In my case they came on the 7th December because I mentioned that I am going to leave the country later in the evening of that day.
* Read your contract carefully and check your obligations regarding giving back the house e.g. paint the walls, even though you have not changed their colour. Ask the agency if you are not sure about what you should do in your flat before you leave. Ask specific questions otherwise they will tell you to read the contract.
* As a general rule, the flat should be returned the way you found it, e.g. if you have paintings on your walls hanged by nails, you need to remove them and close the holes. Same goes for curtains if they were not present when you moved in.

''Personal note: If you know the person who will get into the flat after you (make sure he/she has signed the contract first), you can make arrangements with them. For example, the new tenant had no problem with me leaving the curtains in the flat. In other cases, if you want to leave things behind like furniture or cutlery, you can make a deal with him, with or without money. At any case, you should both agree to let the agency know what things you are leaving behind. If you do not have a direct contact with the new tenant, ask the agency to act as a bridge between you and him/her, or ask for their email.

* Maybe the agency from your new apartment will require a letter from your old flat, make sure you ask them for one, preferably in English. 



== Quitting your contract with the University/Institute earlier==
''Note: this is from personal experience with URZ''

* Speak with group secretary so you can write and sign an official statement saying that you are terminating your contract earlier and provide a short explanation.
* You need to approach the secretary yourself, do not wait until someone approaches you.

== Bürgeramt==
When you entered Germany, you registered yourself in the city's Bürgeramt. You need to unrigester yourself once you decide to leave. This also applies if you are moving within Germany.
* Check online or call them to make sure whether or not you need an appointment to unregister yourself.
* In most cases, you need to visit the Bürgeramt within 7 days prior to your leave.
* Take your identification with you.
* Tell them the exact date you are leaving the country.

== Deutsche Rentenversicherung (pension) ==
If you have a contract with the University/Institute/project, once your contract has ended, the Deutsche Rentenversicherung ends as well.
This is a service that your employer organizes for you when you start working, so they are responsible for unregistering you when the contract is over.
If you would like to move your pension stamps to another country, then:
* Check the [https://www.deutsche-rentenversicherung.de/ Deutsche Rentenversicherung website]. It is available in multiple languages and provides general information.
* Eventually you will need to call them and unfortunately, it is really hard to find someone who speaks English.
* Give details about the country, cause it depends where you are moving:
** Inside EU, you can move your german pension stamps to the new country. 
** Outside EU, there are some countries that have a “collaboration” with Germany and will allow you to take the pension stamps with you.
** In case you can’t take the pension stamps with you, ''you might be eligible'' to take back the money that was deducted from your salary every month and given to your pension. If you are eligible, follow the instructions they give you to claim your money back. You might even be able to take that money back even if you can move the pension stamps to the new country. 
** Please note that if you can move your pension stamps to another country you should notify the corresponding pension insurance about it, once you get a new job.

== [https://www.vbl.de/en/company/ VBL (extra pension)] ==
Same as with Deutsche Rentenversicherung, the website is only available in German and English.
It is not obligatory to have extra pension from VBL, so you might not need to consider this step if you have not at the beginning of your contract.

== Tax declaration ==
If you have registered to a tax declaration office that does your taxes on your behalf, make sure you let them know you are leaving Germany via post. In this case, the 3 months rule does not apply but still do it as soon as possible.

== Health Insurance ==
* Write them a letter 3 months in advance and tell them you are leaving.
* Please be careful cause they might keep you as external participant, so explain to them that you will have insurance in the other country you are going and you will provide them with proof once you move and organize the new health insurance.
* In most cases, they will ask for proof that you are leaving. Therefore, send them a copy of your unregistration from Bürgeramt once you have it. They might ask for a copy from the country you are moving to that shows that you are insured there. 
* In case you are taking prescribed medication or treatment from Germany (once or twice a year free generic blood/urine tests, pap tests, diabetes meds, psychotherapy and medication for any mental disorders, hormones meds etc), they will end once you are no longer registered with a german health insurance provider. Please take good care of this and make appropriate arrangements, in case you still need the medication or treatment.  In other words, any benefits you had in Germany regarding your health will end once your health insurance ends. 

== Student status ==
If you are enrolled as a student, you need to go and unregister yourself. In most universities, you need to fill in an application and hand it over to the person responsible.

== Mobile phone company ==
* Write them a letter 3 months in advance and tell them you are leaving.
* They will ask you for proof that you are leaving Germany, so send them a copy of your unregistration from Bürgeramt once you have it.
* Be careful, you might have two contracts, one for the sim card and one for your mobile phone (if you got one from them) which means you have 2 different contract numbers. Make sure you terminate BOTH, by sending two different letters with your two different contract numbers.
* Follow any details they send you back.
* If you have a contract with them for a mobile phone, they will not take back your phone, but get from your bank account the remaining payment in one payment.
* Based on german law, they can charge you up to 3 months after your contract is over.

== Gym membership ==
* Write them a letter 3 months in advance and tell them you are leaving.
* They will ask you for proof that you are leaving Germany, so send them a copy of your unregistration from Bürgeramt once you have it.
* If you are a member of any other organizations e.g. hair salons, nails salons, clothes companies, let them know you are leaving so they will not be sending you newsletters or new card memberships in your german address. 


== Bank ==
* If you want to keep your account outside Germany, go to a branch and change your address to your new address. It is very important that you give them a new address to reach you e.g to send you your new card. If you have already left the country, you need to send them a written letter with your new address, new phone number and remember to sign the letter.
* If you do not want to keep your bank account, you should ask them what to do to close the account.

== Electricity ==
* Write them a letter 3 months in advance and tell them you are leaving.
* They will ask you for proof that you are leaving Germany, so send them a copy of your unregistration from Bürgeramt once you have it.
* They will send you a form to fill the last day of your residence, in which you will write the final meter reading for your flat and then, you will need to send it back.


== Internet ==
* Write them a letter 3 months in advance and tell them you are leaving.
* They will ask you for proof that you are leaving Germany, so send them a copy of your unregistration from Bürgeramt once you have it.
* Based on german law, they can charge you up to 3 months after your contract is over. They will ask you to send the router back when you leave, including cables etc, and if you do not, they will charge you around 100 euros. So remember to send it back.

== [https://www.rundfunkbeitrag.de/index_ger.html Rund­funk­beitrag] ==
* Fill the [https://www.rundfunkbeitrag.de/buergerinnen_und_buerger/formulare/abmelden/index_ger.html online application].
* It requires a copy of your unregistration from Bürgeramt.
* If for any reason you do not pay this fee, then do not do anything.

title: Letter of Intent
wikitext:
== Letter of Intent (LOI) ==

=== What is a Letter of Intent? ===
For some projects, the project sponsor requires a declaration of intent from the consortium partners and participating companies in the form of a "Letter of Intent" (LOI). In this letter, the relevant party confirms that it will participate in the project and contribute to it if funding is granted. 

=== How is such a letter of intent structured? ===
A letter of intent usually consists of three parts. 
# a brief description of the company and its expertise
# a substantive explanation of why the planned project suits the company in question, how the company can contribute to the planned project and how the company can also benefit from the project
# confirmation that the company will be involved if the project is funded.

The letter of intent should be inserted on the official letterhead and signed with the original signature. 

=== Sample letter of intent (DE) ===

'''Absichtserklärung zur Unterstützung des Projektes XY (Letter of Intent)'''

Sehr geehrte Damen und Herren,

der Arbeitsbereich für Data Science an der Universität Paderborn (DICE) entwickelt Verfahren, die zur Nutzbarmachung großer Datensätze eingesetzt werden können. Dabei liegt der Schwerpunkt des Arbeitsbereichs auf Wissensgraphen. Die Mitglieder der Forschungsgruppe entwickeln unter anderem neuartige Verfahren für die Extraktion, Integration, und Verifikation von strukturierten und unstrukturierten Daten. Weitere Schwerpunkte von DICE sind die Analyse und das Durchsuchen (Information Retrieval, Question Answering, Chatbots) von großen Datenbeständen. Mit dieser Expertise möchten wir unseren Beitrag zum geplanten Projekt leisten. [Ergänzende Erläuterungen, wie der Beitrag zum geplanten Projekt aussieht und warum diese Expertise so wichtig für den Erfolg des Projekts ist]. 

Im Namen des Arbeitsbereichs Data Science bestätige ich, dass wir uns an den geplanten Forschungsaktivitäten im Rahmen des Projekts XY beteiligen und die notwendigen Ressourcen bereitstellen, sofern der Antrag zur Finanzierung kommt.

=== Sample letter of intent (EN) ===

'''Letter of Intent to support the project XY (Letter of Intent)'''

Dear Sir or Madam,

The Department of Data Science at Paderborn University (DICE) develops methods that can be used to harness large data sets. The focus of the research group is on knowledge graphs. Among other things, the members of the research group develop new methods for the extraction, integration and verification of structured and unstructured data. DICE also focuses on the analysis and searching (information retrieval, question answering, chatbots) of large data sets. We would like to use this expertise to contribute to the planned project. [Additional explanations of how the contribution to the planned project looks and why this expertise is so important for the success of the project]. 

On behalf of the Data Science department, I confirm that we will participate in the planned research activities as part of the XY project and provide the necessary resources if the application is approved for funding.

title: Matrix
wikitext:
= Using Matrix = Our Matrix server (chat.dice-research.org) is only available for the members of ZIM groups ag-ngonga and dice-chat-users. However, people from other Matrix servers can be invited to any chat. UPB computer science department has their own server: https://element.cs.uni-paderborn.de/ - which is also integrated with IMT accounts and available for all CS students. More information: https://cs.uni-paderborn.de/rechnerbetrieb-irb/dienstuebersicht/matrix == Installing a Matrix Client == * Clients are listed at https://matrix.org/clients/ * The default client is Element (find it at https://element.io/). == Logging in == Note: This assumes you are using the Riot.im client. If you are using a different client, it will look differently. Once the client is opened, click on the “Sign in” button. In the dialog there is the text “Sign in to your Matrix account on matrix.org”. Next to this text there is a “Change” Button. Once you click this button there should be a text field labeled “Homeserver URL”. Enter the URL https://chat.dice-research.org in this field. This will use our own Matrix server instead of the default one. After that, click on next, enter your IMT username and password and click on “Sign in”. == Joining the group chat == You are automatically added into the main and offtopic group chats. == Starting a Chat with a Person == To start a chat with a person you will have to enter their Matrix id.
A Matrix id consists of the username and the homeserver URL.
In our case id will look like this:
@<username>:chat.dice-research.org
Matrix uses this id format to enable users on different servers to chat with each other.
To start a chat with a person on another Matrix server, enter their Matrix ID. You can find your own Matrix ID by clicking on your name in the top left corner.
You might also be able to add a user via their E-Mail address, if they have enabled discovery via their E-Mail address.
This can be done via the settings.
You are always able to find a user with their id. == Inviting a Person into an existing Room == To invite a Person to a Room, click the "Invite Person" Button at the top of the member list on the right side of the Riot window. A small window will open. You can search for a Person to invite here. Again you can find a Person by their Matrix ID, E-Mail (if they set it) or via their Name (if you share a different Room with them). To invite a Person from a different Homeserver, just enter their Matrix ID. After you added the Person(s) you want to invite press the "Send invite" Button. == Starting a Jitsi conference == The Riot client will use Jitsi to start Group voice and video calls. To start a Jitsi conference simply click the voice or video call button on the right of the message textbox. It should add a Jitsi Widget to the room, which will open a conference on our own Jitsi server. Do not use the Jitsi Widget found under "Manage Integrations", it will use the Jitsi server provided by Riot.im.

wikitext: https://web.archive.org/web/20230228154639im_/https://assets.amuniversal.com/c83440a06d5901301d7d001dd8b71c47 == Laptops == The current university laptop supplier has very limited offers, so we don't get to choose much (only a couple of options makes any sense), but also we don't need to be choosing. Planning and tracking: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1Kp4lK0N-etptIsJbQjjfPXAb2JhDrrY32n-oZN9pBQc/#gid=0 * Always get extended warranty such as "ProSupport Plus mit ProSupport, Accidental Damage, Keep Your Hard Drive und Service Account Manager, 60 Monat(e)" (5 Jahre). * If RAM is replaceable, we can purchase with consideration for a later upgrade if it will be needed (in that case if a laptop has 2 RAM slots, make sure only 1 is used originally). == Servers == Planning and tracking: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1Kp4lK0N-etptIsJbQjjfPXAb2JhDrrY32n-oZN9pBQc/#gid=1536461594 === Requirements === https://hilfe.uni-paderborn.de/Housing_-_Voraussetzungen === Suppliers === Some suppliers who sell servers with GPUs and have useable configuration tools on the websites: * https://www.deltacomputer.com/ * https://www.primeline-solutions.com/de/ * https://www.thomas-krenn.com/de/ Other supplier notes: https://uni-paderborn.sciebo.de/f/755120280 === Configuration === Servers are ordered with a public process through IRB. Example requirements: GPU: 4× PCIe NVidia H100 (94 GB VRAM each) CPU: AMD EPYC Gen 4, 256 MB L3 cache, 64 cores, ≥2.55 GHz base clock rate RAM: 768 GB, ECC, DDR4-3200 Storage: 4× 3.2 TB SSD, PCIe Gen 5 Mixed-use, 3 drive writes per day (DWPD) Sustained 128 KiB Sequential Read >13.5 GB/s Sustained 128 KiB Sequential Write >5.5 GB/s Sustained 4 KiB Random Read > 2M IOPS Sustained 4 KiB Random Write > 500K IOPS 2× 900 GB SSD, PCIe Gen 4 Mixed-use, 3 drive writes per day (DWPD) Sustained 128 KiB Sequential Read ≥5 GB/s Sustained 128 KiB Sequential Write ≥1.4 GB/s Sustained 4 KiB Random Read > 500K IOPS Sustained 4 KiB Random Write > 50K IOPS == Planning == Servers: 4 years Parts: 2-3 years == Price calculation == === Basic price for DELL === brutto_(final)_price = netto_(list)_price * (1 - 0.643) * (1 + 0.07) * 64.3% is our discount from DELL ( varies between Precision/Latitude/Optiplex and Poweredge * 7% is our VAT tax from our DELL supplier, since it's a non-profit === Discounts === ==== NVidia ==== "Discount exists" (and often quite generous), no other details publicly available: https://developer.nvidia.com/education-pricing == Billing == For parts, the bill should NOT include "parts for the servers". Just parts. == Retiring == Out-of-warranty laptops: when they are unusable or broken, retire them (order new one, give old one to IRB).

title: Orders
wikitext:
=Guidelines for Orders / Purchases=

Please follow these steps when making purchases or submitting invoices:

'''1. Invoice Submission:'''
Invoices (esp. from outside Germany) must be submitted to the UPB administration **immediately**, ideally in the **same calendar year** as the invoice date.

'''2. Invoice Address:'''
The invoice **must** be addressed to Universität Paderborn.

'''3. VAT Identification Number:'''
Always include the VAT ID of the University of Paderborn: '''DE811209907''' (esp. in orders outside Germany to avoid double taxation).

'''4. Amazon Purchases:'''
For purchases via Amazon, always use the UPB Amazon Business Account. Contact person: Markus Demandt

==Procurement Scenarios==

'''There are three main procurement scenarios:'''

1. UPB purchases the item directly via the procurement office.

2. You order the item yourself, and the invoice is paid by UPB.

3. You purchase and pay in advance, and then request reimbursement from UPB.

Details and procedures for each scenario can be found here: [https://www.uni-paderborn.de/fileadmin/zv/1-1/uni-intern/Infoblatt_-kurz-_Bedarfsstellen_10-2024.pdf Information sheet (UPB internal access only)])


==Forms and Accounting Sheets==

All necessary forms and accounting sheets are available here: [https://www.uni-paderborn.de/zv/1-1/kontierungsblaetter-und-formulare Forms & Accounting Sheets]

title: Paper writing
wikitext:
This page summarizes some organizational steps for writing a paper. == 1. Starting your paper == '' TODO: Maybe some general hints regarding paper types, lengths, formats, etc. would be good '' * When you start a new paper, please '''add it to the ''In Progress'' tab''' of the [https://uni-paderborn.sciebo.de/f/952907508 list of papers] and define a goal (a conference or a journal) for it. * UPB provides an Overleaf instance at [https://overleaf.uni-paderborn.de/ overleaf.upb.de], which is a good choice if all authors have a UPB login. * Remember the naming convention for papers "CONFERENCE""CONFERENCEYEAR"_"PAPERNAME" (e.g., ISWC2019_FOO) * Remember to name the tex file of your paper the same way as your folder. === Affiliations === The affiliation of our group is (unless stated otherwise): Data Science Group (DICE), Heinz Nixdorf Institute, Department of Computer Science, Paderborn University == 2. Submitting your paper == '' TODO: Maybe some hints regarding blind / double-blind reviews would be good '' Move your paper from the ''In Progress'' table to the ''Submitted'' table in the [https://uni-paderborn.sciebo.de/f/952907508 list of papers]. Prepare travel grant applications at least 4 months in advance (e.g., [https://www2.daad.de/ausland/studieren/stipendium/de/70-stipendien-finden-und-bewerben/?status=&target=&subjectGrps=&daad=&q=kongressreisen&page=1&detail=57369745 DAAD], conference funds, project on which you will travel) == 3. Review results == === Paper acceptance === * If the paper has been accepted, delete your paper from the ''Submitted'' table in the [https://uni-paderborn.sciebo.de/f/952907508 list of papers]. * Check the camera-ready specification of the conference * Provide the VAT number and risk form (see [[Travel]]) * Prepare travel grant applications (e.g., [https://www2.daad.de/ausland/studieren/stipendium/de/70-stipendien-finden-und-bewerben/?status=&target=&subjectGrps=&daad=&q=kongressreisen&page=1&detail=57369745 DAAD], conference funds, project on which you will travel) * Clarify travel arrangements with your group lead (including clear plan for where your traveling funds will come from). * Prepare camera-ready version == 4. Camera-ready version == === 4.1 Acknowledgements === * Which projects should you acknowledge? # Define with the other authors and your group leader which projects fit to the content of your paper or within which project this research has been carried out. # Ask yourself who is going to present the paper and will need to travel. The project from which this person (the one who travels) is paid needs to be added, too. In sum, make sure that relevant projects for your paper (including the project you are paid from if applicable) are acknowledged in your paper as outlined below. '''Failure to do so might result in you not being able to travel''' and hence missing an opportunity to present your work. Further helpful information can be found here: * DFG website on [https://www.dfg.de/en/research-funding/proposal-funding-process/acknowledgements Funding Acknowledgements] * EU webiste on [https://webgate.ec.europa.eu/funding-tenders-opportunities/spaces/OM/pages/1867972/Communicating+your+project+%E2%80%94+Acknowledgement+of+EU+funding#Communicatingyourproject%E2%80%94AcknowledgementofEUfunding-AcknowledgementofEUfunding Funding Acknowledgements] If your paper addresses a specific field from the ''''relevant area'''' or covers topics mentioned in the last column, you can acknowledge this project. It is not an exclusive list, i.e. you may add other projects in reference to what the paper is about. So far the list includes Machine Learning (ML), Natural Language Processing and Data Access (NLP), Benchmarking, Gathering and Cleaning (BGC), Querying and Storage (QS), and Linking (L). Information |- | PC² computing resources || https://pc2.uni-paderborn.de/hpc-services/our-services/forms-documents/acknowledgement/ |} === 4.2 Quality assurance === Provide (1) your group lead and (2) Heidi with your paper at least a week before the submission deadline for a final check. ===4.3 SVN Upload=== Papers have to uploaded to our open SVN following this path pattern: https://svn.dice-research.org/open/papers//. ====4.3.1 Upload Paper Source Code==== All papers should be uploaded as ''compilable'' tex in our SVN. This includes * All tex files of the paper * All tex files of the presentation of the paper * All additional files and images needed to compile them ====4.3.2 Make PDFs Publicly Available==== In addition, you may want to make the paper and the presentation publicly available. This can be done via our SVN as well. 1. First check, if you want to add a comment "preprint version" to the PDF. Adding a title to the filename is recommended (see below). 2. After the paper has been finalized, its PDF should be uploaded to our SVN as file ending with public.pdf. This will make the paper publicly available. The path of the PDF should follow the pattern:
https://svn.dice-research.org/open/papers///public.pdf
This will lead to the paper being available via the following URL:
https://papers.dice-research.org///public.pdf
Note: The mirror will be synced every full hour, so you might have to wait up to an hour until your paper is available publicly. Additionally, you should execute the following command in the papers directory to add the information that the paper is a PDF file:
svn propset svn:mime-type application/pdf public.pdf You may want to do the same with the paper presentation slides to be able to link them later on (see bibtex description below). === 4.4 Updating Bibsonomy === We are using Bibsonomy to keep track of our papers. Therefore, you should add your new paper to make sure that it appears on the dice page. ==== Update dice.bib ==== Therefore, you should add your paper to our [https://github.com/dice-group/dice-website/blob/develop/data/bib/dice.bib dice.bib file] on github. The file contains nearly all papers of the DICE group. '''Please be careful when editing the dice.bib file!''. We suggest the adoption of JabRef application for including your papers and parsing the correctly.' A typical entry looks like the following: 
@inproceedings{qudus2023temporalfc,
	address = {Cham},
	author = {Qudus, Umair and R{\"o}der, Michael and Kirrane, Sabrina and Ngomo, Axel-Cyrille Ngonga},
	biburl = {https://www.bibsonomy.org/bibtex/2ec2f0b9ee7ca0c1c6ef1d8fbcd7262e4/dice-research},
	booktitle = {The Semantic Web -- ISWC 2023},
	editor = {R. Payne, Terry and Presutti, Valentina and Qi, Guilin and Poveda-Villalónt, María and Stoilos, Giorgos and Hollink, Laura and Kaoudi, Zoi and Cheng, Gong and Juanzi Li},
	keywords = {knowgraphs enexa sailproject nebulaproject dice ngonga saleem roeder qudus},
	publisher = {Springer International Publishing},
	doi = {10.1007/978-3-031-47240-4_25},
	isbn = {978-3-031-47239-8},
	title = {TEMPORALFC: A Temporal Fact Checking approach over Knowledge Graphs},
	presentation = {https://svn.dice-research.org/open/papers/2023/ISWC_TemporalFC/presentation/TemporalFC-presentation/TemporalFC_presentation.pdf},
	url = {https://papers.dice-research.org/2023/ISWC_TemporalFC/public.pdf},
	year = {2023},
	video = {https://videolectures.net/videos/iswc2023_qudus_temporalfc_fact},
	bdsk-url-1 = {https://papers.dice-research.org/2023/ISWC_TemporalFC/public.pdf},
	bdsk-url-2 = {https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-47240-4_25}
}
It can be seen that the general bibtex information is listed but also some special keys are used that our website relies on. The picture on the right shows an example of the bibtex above rendered by our website. The table below lists these keywords and their effect [[Datei:Example paper on web page.png|mini|An example of a paper rendered by our website. Please note the different icons that the website supports.]] {| class="wikitable" |+ Bibtex keys and their usage in our website |- ! Key !! Effect !! Description |- | title || Title of the paper || |- | url || Title link || If this keyword is present, the title is rendered as link to this URL. This should be used to link the paper to its PDF or the publisher's page of the paper. |- | doi || The paper's DOI || If this keyword is present, a small DOI icon is added to the paper and is linked to the URL with the given DOI. |- | keywords || Paper is shown on website || Please make sure to put the correct keywords for * our group dice → paper becomes visible on the website * projects, e.g., knowgraphs enexa sailproject nebulaproject → paper is linked to projects * authors, e.g., ngonga saleem roeder qudus → paper is available on the personal pages of the authors Keywords can be found in the ttl files of the project or person that you want to link to the paper. |- | bdsk-url-1 || Link to the PDF || If this keyword is present, a small PDF icon is added to the paper and is linked to this URL. |- | video || Video of the presentation || If this keyword is present, a small video icon is added to the paper and is linked to this URL. |- | presentation || Presentation slides || If this keyword is present, a small slides icon is added to the paper and is linked to this URL. |- | year || || The year is used for the filtering functionality on the website. |} about the paper are listed as well as the link to the public.pdf file in the DICE SVN. '''Note''': when using URLs that are based on DOIs of Springer, please remove the backslash, i.e., the following URL is wrong and will avoid the successful deployment of our website: 
url = {https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-00382-0\_44}
Instead, the backslash in front of the underscore has to be removed so that our website can process the URL later on. After editing the dice.bib, create a pull request on github to merge your changes into the master branch of our website. Note that automatic checks will ensure that the dice.bib file can be parsed correctly after your changes. ''Ensure that the checks pass and fix the reported problems if they don't''. After your changes are merged into the master branch by one of the website administrators, you updated bibliography information is uploaded to bibsonomy and integrated into our website, automatically. === 4.5 Publish your results === * '''UPB RIS''': Add your paper to Research Information System [https://ris.upb.de/ ris.upb.de]. ** If you can not login, activate the RIS service at [https://serviceportal.uni-paderborn.de/ sp.upb.de]. ** When editing your paper in RIS, add ''Data Science'' as ''Department'' to have it in the [https://ris.uni-paderborn.de/record?cql=department%3D574 list of data science publications] * '''Social Media''': Send a message to Franzi, she will prepare a post for your paper. * '''Data (optional)''': Check if you generated data which could be useful for further research. You can provide data on the [[DiceResources|Hobbit FTP server]] and publish the related metadata using our [[CKAN]]. If you require a DOI for your data, you could also use [https://zenodo.org/ Zenodo]. === 4.6 Cleanup === Please remove your finished and published paper from the [https://uni-paderborn.sciebo.de/f/952907508 list of papers]. == 5. Paper Presentation == * Prepare your presentation at least 2 weeks before your conference * Presentation templates can be found in our SVN: [https://svn.dice-research.org/open/templates/beamer/ new template] [https://svn.dice-research.org/open/papers/resources/slidedecks_template/ old template] * Your presentation is part of the paper. Add it to a subfolder named "Slides" in the SVN folder with the final version of your paper * Review your presentation with your group leader * Carry out at least one live '''presentation rehearsal''' and pay attention for the feedback * Pay attention not exceed to the presentation time of your session which normally around 20 minutes presentation and 10 minutes for questions (check your conference page for the exact times) * Hint for a professional presentation ** Do not forget to mention your co-author the first slide, if any ** Do not forget to motivate your work at the very beginning ** Attract the attention of your audience by presenting a running example ** ''"A picture is worth a thousand words"'' i.e., use less text more images/figures/tables ** Try to limit your text to maximum of 7 lines per slide and 7 words per line and do not write complete sentences ** Focus on your work/evaluation not in background/related work ** Do not forget the '''Thanks Slide''' at the very end of your presentation For more details, see our [https://svn.dice-research.org/open/teaching/2021_ws/RAKG/03%20-%20scientific%20presentation/Scientific_presentation.pdf scientific presentation slides] === Fix for laggy PDF produced by beamer === When you use our official latex beamer template you are likely to come across laggy pdfs due to resolution of embedded bitmap images. You can fix this by applying this command to your final pdf: 
$ gs -sDEVICE=pdfwrite -dCompatibilityLevel=1.4 -dPDFSETTINGS=/printer -dNOPAUSE -dQUIET -dBATCH -sOutputFile=slides_reduced.pdf slides.pdf
You can also shrink your embedded images in the beginning. See the image resolution: 
$ identify DICE_White.png
DICE_White.png PNG 11790x5309 11790x5309+0+0 8-bit sRGB 378853B 0.000u 0:00.000
This image is way too big and needs to be resized: 
$ mogrify -resize 10% DICE_White.png
You will not always see this with '''ls -h''', since e.g. png compression largely reduces file sizes of monochromatic images as above but when it gets embedded in pdf this compression is sometimes lost.

== Organization at the UPB ==

'''''Preliminary version from March 1, 2019'''''

For receiving the PhD grade from the UPB, there are two major steps required. 

=== 1. Admission ===

The PhD board has to check whether the student fulfills the prerequisites for a PhD. The required documents can be found on the [https://cs.uni-paderborn.de/en/studies/doctoral-committee-computer-science UPB web page](at the bottom of the page).

Based on the submitted documents, the PhD board will decide whether you are allowed to submit your thesis.

After a positive response from the PhD board, you can register yourself as student of the university. Note that this is '''not mandatory''' and you are free to decide whether you want to become a student or not.

Read [https://www.uni-paderborn.de/en/zv/4-5/staff-development/supervision-agreements here] more about the supervision agreement between you and your supervisor. 

=== 2. Submission ===

After the PhD board admitted the student, the PhD thesis can be submitted. The required documents can be found on the [https://cs.uni-paderborn.de/en/studies/doctoral-committee-computer-science UPB web page](at the bottom of the page).

== Promotion regulations ==

See 'Promotion' at https://cs.uni-paderborn.de/en/studies/audit-matters

title: PhD hat
wikitext:
It became a tradition of the DICE group that a PhD student receives a special (funny) PhD hat after they successfully pass their defense. This PhD hat should be tinkered by members of the DICE group (ideally, without the PhD student noticing). The '''hat''' is given to the PhD student (the '''target''') directly after the successful defense so that they can wear it when making photos. It typically comes with a '''card''' and a '''gift'''.

==The Hat Agent==

The group chooses a hat agent, i.e., a person responsible for creating the hat. This may be the PhD student that is most likely the next student to defend their thesis. However, the process is not well defined.

==Planning Phase==

[[Datei:Buttons.jpg|mini|Buttons are an easy way to attach logos of projects to the side of the hat.]]

Creating the hat typically needs to be planned. The hat agent may organize meetings with group members that know the target well and create a list of possible topics that might be possible to be covered by the hat. Typical points that are covered by a hat are the following (this is a non-exhaustive list):
* Research topic of the target
** Figures or objects from the thesis (or related to it)
** Figures or objects from papers (or related to them)
** Objects / Logos related to tools that the target implemented or worked with
** Objects / Logos related to projects that the target worked on
* Countries that the target visited during their PhD
* Objects related to the personality of the target
** Hobbies
** Food
** Habits
** Events that happened during the PhD

==Tinkering Phase==

[[Datei:Clips.png|mini|Clips are typically used to attach a carton basement to the bought hat.]]

The hat agent typically orders a hat that is used as "basement". Especially the top but also the sides of the hat may be decorated. A group of volunteers creates and adds the decorations based on the previous discussions. This is typically done together in one or several sessions.

==Organizational Details==

* It might be a good idea to create an own private chat room for the hat creation process and invite everybody, except the target.
* The hat agent should organize the card that can be signed by group members. Note that not all group members are always available. Hence, a period of 2 weeks is a good way to ensure that a lot of people can sign the card.
* Over the whole creation process, the hat agent should keep track of costs that they had to cover.
* The hat agent should also start to collect money from group members as soon as the card can be signed. The money has two purposes: 1) it should cover the costs of the hat and 2) it should be used for a gift (typically, a voucher) that is given to the target together with the hat and the card.

==Examples==

<gallery>
PhD Hat Micha.jpg|Micha's PhD hat
PhD Hat Hamada.png|Hamada's Phd hat during the creation process
PhD Hat Demir.jpg|Demir with his PhD hat after the defense
PhD Hat Abdullah.png|Abdullah's PhD hat
PhD Hat Rene.jpg|René and Umair with René's PhD hat after the defense
</gallery>

title: Proposal writing
wikitext:
[[Datei:Grafik Proposal Writing Timeline3.png|mini|rechts|600px|Proposal writing workflow]] '''Getting Started:''' # '''Find a suitable call''' that matches the scientific ambition and strategic goals of your idea. A list of platforms with national and EU funding opportunities is available [[Research_project_proposals|here]]. # '''Reach out to colleagues''' who could contribute scientifically, technically or through use cases. # '''Analyse the call in depth''' and map your concrete ideas, methods and expected results to the expected outcomes, the scope, and the impact requirements of the call. # '''Seek support from DICE Research Management''' (for instance, w.r.t. funding rules, call requirements, forms and budgets, consortium data, ethics and data management, timelines and submission logistics). # '''Streamline your proposal writing workflow''' (see image for the time frame and steps recommended for an EU grant application). ''Further tips on the individual steps and sections of an EU grant application can be found below.''
== Delevop your idea == [[Datei:Program structure of Horizon Europe.png|mini|rechts|600px]] '''Horizon Europe''' is structured in three program pillars (Pillar I: Execellent Science, Pillar II: Global Challenges and European Industrial Competitiveness, Pillar III: Innovative Europe). You can find more information [https://research-and-innovation.ec.europa.eu/document/download/9224c3b4-f529-4b48-b21b-879c442002a2_en?filename=ec_rtd_he-investing-to-shape-our-future.pdf here]. === Gather information === * Align your idea(s) and the framing of your proposal with the EU's vision behind the call you are interested in. ** Applicable [https://research-and-innovation.ec.europa.eu/funding/funding-opportunities/funding-programmes-and-open-calls/horizon-europe/horizon-europe-work-programmes_en Work programme] / Destination *** Material to read for [https://research-and-innovation.ec.europa.eu/funding/funding-opportunities/funding-programmes-and-open-calls/horizon-europe/cluster-1-health_en Cluster 1: Health] *** Material to read for [https://research-and-innovation.ec.europa.eu/funding/funding-opportunities/funding-programmes-and-open-calls/horizon-europe/cluster-2-culture-creativity-and-inclusive-society_en Cluster 2: Culture, Creativity and Inclusive society] *** Material to read for [https://research-and-innovation.ec.europa.eu/funding/funding-opportunities/funding-programmes-and-open-calls/horizon-europe/cluster-3-civil-security-society_en Cluster 3: Civil security for society] *** Material to read for [https://research-and-innovation.ec.europa.eu/funding/funding-opportunities/funding-programmes-and-open-calls/horizon-europe/cluster-4-digital-industry-and-space_en Cluster 4: Digital, Industry and Space] *** Material to read for [https://research-and-innovation.ec.europa.eu/funding/funding-opportunities/funding-programmes-and-open-calls/horizon-europe/cluster-5-climate-energy-and-mobility_en Cluster 5: Climate, Energy and Mobility] *** Material to read for [https://research-and-innovation.ec.europa.eu/funding/funding-opportunities/funding-programmes-and-open-calls/horizon-europe/cluster-6-food-bioeconomy-natural-resources-agriculture-and-environment_en Cluster 6: Food, Bioeconomy, Natural Resources, Agriculture and Environment] *** Material to read for [https://research-and-innovation.ec.europa.eu/funding/funding-opportunities/funding-programmes-and-open-calls/horizon-europe/research-infrastructures_en Research Infrastructures] ** Horizon Europe Strategic Plan [https://op.europa.eu/en/web/eu-law-and-publications/publication-detail/-/publication/3c6ffd74-8ac3-11eb-b85c-01aa75ed71a1 2021-2024] and [https://op.europa.eu/en/publication-detail/-/publication/b3baec75-fdd0-11ed-a05c-01aa75ed71a1/language-en/format-PDF/source-287596143 2025-2027] (i.e. current funding programme for research and innovation) ** [https://research-and-innovation.ec.europa.eu/funding/funding-opportunities/funding-programmes-and-open-calls/horizon-europe/eu-missions-horizon-europe_en EU Missions] === Avoid pitfalls === * Check previous evaluation letters for criticism * Check call for eligibility, award and ranking criteria ** Check if you need to contribute to the implementation of a new European industrial or AI strategy or research agenda (see section above). ** Check if you need to show a differentiation from and synergies with other EU programmes such as „Digital Europe“ and the space programme in the sense of a complementarity with Horizon Europe. ** Check if there are specific topic conditions included in the call (such as internationality or collaboration with SSH disciplines).
== Plan your proposal writing == * Check out the list of recommended steps for writing a grant proposal in our {{Sciebo|952858062}} ** The template helps you plan your internal '''deadlines''' (please enter the submission date at the top of the table, deadlines are then calculated automatically). ** The template describes '''milestones''' prior to submission and indicates '''responsibilities''' for milestones and tasks. * Ask DICE Research Management for the most up-to-date proposal template (available in LaTex) == Build your consortium == === Select partners === * Think about choice of partners ('pedigree' and fitness to idea) * Think about the work packages you need in order to achieve your planned goals and allocate appropriate partners * Develop a rough work plan at this stage === Find partners === * Participate in brokerage events published e.g. by the EU [https://research-innovation-community.ec.europa.eu/events here] * The German NCP ''Digital and Industrial Technologies'' provides the following information: ** Collection of support services and events on finding partners or joining a promising consortium [https://www.nks-dit.de/aktuelles/news/wie_werde_ich_partner_in_einem_konsortium here] ** Cooperation profiles from parties interested in participating in current calls from Cluster 4 or AI-related ones [https://www.nks-dit.de/service/cooperationprofiles here] * Check the specific call page at the [https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/calls-for-proposals?isExactMatch=true&status=31094501,31094502,31094503&frameworkProgramme=43108390&order=DESC&pageNumber=1&pageSize=50&sortBy=startDate EU website] for partner search announcements * Check partners DICE has worked with in similar projects before === Eligible Countries === Before finalising your consortium, verify the eligibility status of all partner countries. *Consult the official list of EU Member States and Associated Countries in the Horizon Europe Programme Guide [https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/docs/2021-2027/common/guidance/list-3rd-country-participation_horizon-euratom_en.pdf here]. *''Associated Countries'' are generally fully eligible for EU funding. No national co-funding is required. They have the same rights and obligations as EU partners (e.g. funding rates, reporting requirements, contractual rules), as they contribute to the Horizon Europe budget. However, eligibility may vary depending on the specific call. Some calls include additional geographical requirements or restrictions. Always check the call text carefully. * Note that some countries are associated only to specific programme parts (''Pillars'') * If in doubt, consult Research Management before confirming partners. == Write your proposal == === Template === * Request the current template from Research Management. Do not use old templates, as specific calls might use different page limits or have individual requirements. * Plan your proposal according to the correct page limits. From 2026 onwards, the standard limits are: ** 40 pages for actual cost RIA and IA ** 45 pages for lump sum RIA and IA * Carefully read the instructions for each section in the template and follow them closely. * Do not remove template tags or markers. Some templates contain light grey tags or hidden structural markers. These are required by the European Commission to enable automated processing, indexing, and faster evaluation of the document. Even if they appear redundant or purely technical, they must remain in the final submitted version. ==== Excellence Section ==== * Clear and measurable objectives * KPIs must be quantified. (What do you measure?) * Key words from the call (or equivalent formulations) must be included (otherwise loss of points in review). ==== Impact Section ==== * Impact has to be measured; it has to be explained how this should be done. * Updates for Impact Section, applicable from 2026 onwards: ** The element “likely scale and significance of the contributions from the project” has been removed from the Impact evaluation criterion. ** In Section 2.1, applicants are no longer required to separately describe the general scientific, economic, and societal expected impacts, as these are already reflected in the topic’s expected impact. ** The subsection “Project’s pathways towards impact” has been simplified. The previously mandatory impact summary tables are now optional and may be removed if not used by applicants. ==== Implementation Section (Work Plan) ==== * Align milestones with KPIs from excellence section (make your results verifiable). ==== Important notes==== '''Check Requirements''' *e.g. AT LEAST three use cases; TWO examples PER application area, focus on ONE application area... *is a specific field of application required or is a generic applicability of the proposed technological solution to be shown? *pay attention to the extent to which existing technologies may be used *if specified, note which technology readiness level (TLR) is requested in the call *is an exploitation plan for after the project required? '''Check feasibility''' *do not promise anything in the proposal that is not realistically achievable within the project duration and with the requested funds / non-realistic settings '''Not wanted by reviewers and experts''' *"proposals that focus on low impact sectors with little potential to deliver economic or societal benefits" *"academic exercises with limited potential for commercial exploitation of the results after the end of the project" *"proposals with limited ambition delivering only incremental progress over the scientific state of the art" (the reviewers and experts look very closely at State of the Art) *in calls with human-centric approach: a lack of limited end user involvement '''Check form''' *do not deviate from admin/formal requirements: e. g. transfer of essential information to annexes to overcome page limits, font size and formatting imposed by the templates. If graphics are used, they should be clearly legible! *include abbreviation list (helps reviewers) *include linked table of contents (recommended) '''Check budget and work distribution''' *ensure consistency between budget and work plan *ensure work-related distribution of budget among partners *Distribution of work should reflect collaborative character of a European consortium. *in the case of international cooperation (no funding by the EU): this partner should provide a committment that if the proposal is selected the funding will be available === Project Management (if you will be coordinator of the project) === * Aspects to cover for PM: coordination of consortium, financial administration, controlling/quality management, reporting, data management, ethics/GDPR compliance * Create budget and Gantt chart * Identify genuine risks and describe adequate management (Todo: anything else??) * Define governance structure (define roles, leads, boards, managers --> create image) * Define management style/ school (Todo: Specifics??) * Legal/admin data of UPB for EU grant proposals can be found [[Research_project_EU|here]]. === Costs === ==== PM Rate ==== The '''PM rate for research assistants''' can vary depending on the members of your team and their years of experience in research. Salary group E13 between levels 2 and 5, all of which are specified in the [https://oeffentlicher-dienst.info/tv-l/allg/ collective agreement] for the public sector in the German federal states (TV-L), often applies. The PM rates are currently set for the period from April 2026 to January 2028; after that, a wage increase should be calculated again (if possible). All figures listed below represent gross costs for employers. {| class="wikitable" |+ PM Rate for research assistants (TV-L E13/2-5) |- ! E13 !! 2026 !! 2027 !! 2028 (only January) !! 2028 (from February onwards plus 3.5%) !! 2029 (plus 3.5%) |- | Level 2 || 6,762.38 € || 6,875.08 € || 6,966.60 € || 7,210.43€ || 7,462.79 € |- | Level 3 || 7,107.78 € || 7,226.24 € || 7,322.43 € || 7,578.72 € || 7,843.97 € |- | Level 4 || 7,778.80 € || 7,908.44 € || 8,013.72 € || 8,294.20 € || 8,584.49 € |- | Level 5 || 8,706.40 € || 8,851.51 € || 8,968.33 € || 9,283.26 € || 9,608.17 € |} You can calculate average values per year for different groups of employees, e.g., from level 2 and 3 for doctoral students and from level 4 and 5 for postdoctoral researchers. You can '''round up to the nearest hundred'''. Personnel costs in EU proposal do not have to reflect exact actual costs but can be based on favorable but reasonable estimates. They should be verifiable through the [https://dashboard.tech.ec.europa.eu/qs_digit_dashboard_mt/public/sense/app/10526974-8664-4f61-8b86-8ecd3a3c8aec/sheet/4304a311-3099-4fe1-97ed-41f6f2782651/state/analysis EU dahsboard] (esp. for lump-sum projects). The cost rate should be increased by the overhead costs in case they are not added separately (usually 25% for EU funding). Often they are, however, entered independently. The monthly costs for a student assistant (usually one part-time student per full-time researcher) amounts to a gross wage of 702.50 € for 9.5 h/w. ==== Travel Costs ==== ==== Equipment Costs ==== == Policy Obligations == === Institutional Requirements === * Inclusive Gender Equality Plan (GEP) ([https://www.uni-paderborn.de/gleichstellung/gleichstellungsbeauftragte/angebote/beratungsangebot-zu-gleichstellungsaspekten-bei-der-beantragung-von-forschungsprojekten/genderaspekte-im-horizon-europa here]) * Data Management ([https://www.uni-paderborn.de/forschung/forschungsservice-und-beratung/forschungsdaten here]) * Open access strategy ([https://www.ub.uni-paderborn.de/unterstuetzung/open-access here]) * Research Ethics ([https://www.uni-paderborn.de/forschung/gute-wissenschaftliche-praxis here]) * GDPR compliance and Data Protection Officers ([https://www.uni-paderborn.de/universitaet/datenschutz here]) * Text samples for cross-cutting priorities from UPB funding advisors ([https://www.uni-paderborn.de/forschung/forschungsservice-und-beratung#downloads here]) === Open Science === * [https://rea.ec.europa.eu/open-science_en#open-science-and-the-proposal-application Questions & Answers] on Open Science requirements under Horizon Europe to help coordinators better understand and respect this contractual obligation. === Gender === ''[To be extended. title: Python
wikitext: == How to == === Create a separate python environment === python -m venv path-to-where-to-create-a-new-venv You are not required to use the provided activate script. your-venv/bin/python and your-venv/bin/pip can be used directly. https://docs.python.org/3/library/venv.html === Install python modules === ==== OS packages ==== Most popular packages can be found in packages provided with your system. They would be available outside of venvs. For example, in Debian [https://tqdm.github.io/ tqdm] can be installed with apt install [https://packages.debian.org/stable/python3-tqdm python3-tqdm]. ==== pip ==== Use your-venv/bin/pip install to install the packages. All required packages for your project with their concrete versions should be managed with [https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/user_guide/#requirements-files requirements files] or other solutions. === Use a different python version === ... == conda == https://www.anaconda.com/blog/update-on-anacondas-terms-of-service-for-academia-and-research older content: '''We are NOT allowed to use the default package repository (Anaconda) used by conda, as our usage requires a paid license. See more in ToS: https://legal.anaconda.com/policies/en?name=terms-of-service''' In practice it means that the usage of conda install in the default configuration of conda is not allowed. You can still use conda to manage environments and use other package repositories, such as https://conda-forge.org/, after confirming that the corresponding ToS and license allow us to use the repository. On our experiment servers (not on VMs) we have [https://github.com/conda-forge/miniforge miniforge (a variant of conda)] installed which uses conda-forge by default, but you should confirm that with conda config --show-sources, as it is possible to misconfigure or misuse it. The easier approach is to just avoid using conda if you can. === conda in source code === When publishing your code, make sure on each use of conda install you explicitly specify a channel using --channel option.

title: Remote Access
wikitext:
= SSH = All IRB managed VMs and Servers as well as most other VMs and Servers can be reached via SSH (Secure SHell). There are different methods that can be used to authenticate to an SSH server, the two most common being passwords and ssh keys. While passwords are self-explanatory, ssh keys are not. == Authentication == === SSH Keys === SSH keys work by using a public and private key scheme, where the server knows the public key(s) for a user and the client proves possession of the private key. To generate a key pair use the ssh-keygen -t rsa -b 4096 command. This generates an 4096 bit RSA key pair. You can either do this by hand or use the ssh-copy-id @ command. To install the key by hand you have to copy the contents of the ~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub file into the ~/.ssh/authorized_keys file on the server(s) you want to login to. The public key file will contain one line text that will look like this ssh-rsa AAAAB3Nz[...]SlNt0jtkEr1Q29SD/ @. Append this line to the ~/.ssh/authorized_keys file on the target server(s). You might have to create the file and folder. === Kerberos === Another authentication method is kerberos. Kerberos works by authenticating to a central server (for example with a password) in exchange for a ticket. This ticket can then be used to login to the target server (if it has been setup for kerberos auth). All IRB managed VMs and Servers are setup for Kerberos auth. To setup your local system for Kerberos refer to this page: https://hilfe.uni-paderborn.de/Single-Sign-On_einrichten_unter_Linux It boils down to executing sudo apt install krb5-user; sudo wget -4 https://download.uni-paderborn.de/pc/configs/kerberos/krb5.conf -O /etc/krb5.conf once and then using kinit to login. To use Kerberos with ssh, add the -K flag to your command. Example: ssh -K raki.cs.upb.de == Important Information for IRB managed VMs and Servers == By default IRB managed VMs and Servers do not allow password auth. Instead SSH keys or Kerberos should be used. To setup your SSH key(s) you can connect via the IRB sshgate (ssh @sshgate.cs.upb.de), it will automatically authenticate you using Kerberos. You can then connect to your desired target and insert your public key into the ~/.ssh/authorized_keys file. == SSH tunnel into UPB == To access servers that are only available inside the UPB network, you need to tunnel in. Connect with ssh @sshgate.cs.uni-paderborn.de . You are prompted to enter your password. Now you have a terminal inside the upb. You can now connect to any other server by running ssh .cs.uni-paderborn.de. If the Server or VM you are connecting to is managed by the IRB, you will not be prompted for your Password again since the sshgate automatically handles Kerberos Authentication. If you cannot connect, you are probably not allowed to access the server. You can also shorten these two steps into one command: ssh -J @sshgate.cs.uni-pderborn.de .cs.uni-paderborn.de If you need to forward a port form the remote server to your local machine (for example to access a service running on the server), you can do so with the following command: ssh -J @sshgate.cs.uni-paderborn.de -L localhost::localhost: .cs.uni-paderborn.de Backup ssh host: sshgate2.cs.uni-paderborn.de == Copying files from and to servers == The usage of ftp to transfer files is discouraged, as the protocol does not support encryption of files or credentials. Instead something like sftp should be used. === scp === For simple file transfers, `scp` (Secure CoPy) can be used. You can use it like this `scp `, where source and target are a local path and a remote path in the form of `@:`. For example, to copy a file named `example` in the current directory to your home directory on a server use `scp example user@server:~/`. To copy the file back to your current directory you can use `scp user@server:~/example ./` === rsync === A more advanced utility is `rsync`. rsync uses the same path notation as `scp`, but has more features. `rsync` compares source and destination files and only transfers the difference between the two. This can be very useful if you are transferring very large files over a unstable connection, as `rsync` can resume the transfer. For rsync to work, it has to be installed on both systems. However all IRB managed servers, as well as most other servers have `rsync` installed. By default `rsync` is silent. To enable a progress report, call `rsync with the `-P` flag. To copy a whole directory use the `-r` flag. Important note: Unlike the GNU corutils `cp` command, `rsync` uses the BSD convention for paths. A trailing slash on a path will copy the contents of that directory, instead of the directory itself. For more information on `rsync` see `man rsync` === Mounting the filesystem via SSH === With this shell alias you can use the command upbmnt to mount your UPB space on your local machine: alias upbmnt='sshfs @sshgate.cs.upb.de:/upb/users/// ' == Example SSH configuration == === Automatically connect with sshgate to all .cs.upb.de servers === In your ~/.ssh/config: 
Host *.cs.uni-paderborn.de
    GSSAPIAuthentication yes
    GSSAPIClientIdentity your_imt_username@UNI-PADERBORN.DE
    PasswordAuthentication no
    PreferredAuthentications=gssapi-with-mic
    PubkeyAuthentication no
    User your_imt_username

Host *.cs.uni-paderborn.de !sshgate.* !sshgate2.* !git.*
    ProxyJump sshgate.cs.uni-paderborn.de
Source: https://cs.uni-paderborn.de/en/irb/services/translate-to-english-login-per-kerberos === Automatically run kinit if needed === In your ~/.ssh/config: 
Match host *.cs.uni-paderborn.de exec "klist -s ||zenity --title 'Connecting to %h' --password |kinit -V -l 16h your_imt_username@UNI-PADERBORN.DE"
Works with background ssh connections (for example, from your editor), asks for the password in a graphical window. Make sure zenity is installed. == SOCKS5 proxy == 
# ~/.config/systemd/user/upb-tunnel-proxy.socket
[Socket]
ListenStream=127.0.0.1:7059
[Install]
WantedBy=sockets.target

# ~/.config/systemd/user/upb-tunnel-proxy.service
[Unit]
BindsTo=upb-tunnel.service
After=upb-tunnel.service
[Service]
ExecStart=/lib/systemd/systemd-socket-proxyd --exit-idle-time=500s localhost:7060

# ~/.config/systemd/user/upb-tunnel.service
[Unit]
StopWhenUnneeded=true
[Service]
ExecStart=-/usr/bin/ssh -qxNT -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes -o ControlMaster=no -D 7060 sshgate.cs.uni-paderborn.de
ExecStartPost=/bin/sleep 5
= Remote desktop = Working with a graphical environment on a VM can be done via the vSphere web ui, but this not fast. The VMware workstation offers better performance, but requires a license. An alternative could be [https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/spice/x11spice x11spice] which allows connecting to a running X11 session via the SPICE protocol. The [https://git.cs.upb.de/dice-infrastructure/x11spice-setup x11spice-setup] can be used to setup x11spice and connect to a remote machine. Further documentation can be found in the repository. = VPN = See [[VPN]]

title: Research project AZA
wikitext:
=== Proposal Management ===

==== ''''Projektskizze''''====

Involve DICE Research Management (Franziska, Nadine) and provide proposal details [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1-yEx9GRIrDyJQ2AQOJFQgkTn8B8PrHSA7DKkSSIDKg0/edit#gid=147559712 '''here'''].  

===== Tips =====

# '''UPB legal/administrative data''' can be found in [https://www.uni-paderborn.de/fileadmin/zv/2-2/Muster_AZAP_Ausfuellhilfe.pdf '''Ausfüllhinweise easyOnline'''].
# 
# If funding provides for '''overhead costs''' (often applicable to universities in national funding programmes --> check call details), your budget must also reflect these costs. You can calculate them separately or as part of each direct cost category (often a flat rate of 20% of your direct costs). 
#
# Personnel costs are calculated on the basis of UPB's [[Research_project_AZA#Person-month_.28PM.29_Rate|PM rates]].
# 
# Check with funding authority which type of signature is needed on 'Skizze' (from legal representative or from head of DICE). A signature from the legal representative requires more time as submission involves UPB's research service center.

===== EuroStars =====

# A commitment form must be signed by the legal representative of UPB (i.e. Vice-President). 
# 
# Contact UPB's research service center which will obtain the signature for you. Please provide the following information to them:
#
 * What are the names of the project partners? 
 * When is the project expected to start? 
 * What is the planned budget for UPB?
 * Is there a flat rate for overhead costs and how much is it?
 * What is the project about (= title and abstract)?

==== ''''Vollantrag'''' ====

Universities must fill out the AZAP budget form via the [https://foerderportal.bund.de/easyonline/formularassistent.jsf '''easy-Online'''] platform. Contact DICE Research Management (Franziska, Nadine) for support.

===== Person-month (PM) Rate ===== 

'''In full proposals''' funded by one of the German ministries, the '''PM rate for research assistants''' is generally limited to salary group E13 level 2 (E13-2), which is specified in the [https://oeffentlicher-dienst.info/tv-l/allg/ collective agreement] for the public sector in the German federal states (TV-L). The PM rate for E13-2 is currently set  for the period from April 2026 to January 2028; after that a wage increase should be calculated again (if possible). All figures listed below represent gross costs for employers. 

{| class="wikitable"
|+ PM Rate for research assistants (TV-L E13-2)
|-
! Period !! Monthly rate !! Yearly rate 
|-
| 2026 (monthly rate valid from April onwards) || 6,762.38 € || 80,595.98 € 
|-
| 2027 || 6,875.08 € || 82,501.01 €
|-
| 2028 (January only) || 6,966.60 € || see below 
|-
| 2028 (est. with 3.5% increase) || 7,210.43 € || 86,281.33 €
|-
| 2029 (est. with 3.5% increase) || 7,462.79 € || 89,553.54 €
|}

In '''project outlines''' the cost rate should be increased by the overhead costs if a flate rate for such costs is provided for in the call (usually 20% or 22% for national funding).

In '''project outlines''' you may also increase the monthly cost rate by the monthly costs for a student assistant (usually one part-time student per full-time researcher, i.e. gross costs of 702.50 € for 9.5 h/w)  to make sure your personnel costs will be sufficient.

The '''DFG''' will ask you to calculate your personnel costs on the basis of their general cost rates which are yearly updated. Cost rates for 2026 can be checked [https://www.dfg.de/resource/blob/368644/60-12-2026-de.pdf here].

===== Check List =====
# Use the personnel cost rates caculator from UPB's research services for planning personnel costs. The excel sheet ''''Kalkulation der Personalkostensätze'''' is available in their download area [https://www.uni-paderborn.de/forschung/forschungsservice-und-beratung/bundesministerien '''here'''].
# 
# Read their instructions PDF ([https://www.uni-paderborn.de/fileadmin/zv/2-2/Muster_AZAP_Ausfuellhilfe.pdf '''Ausfüllhinweise easyOnline''']) to fill out the easy-Online form with correct '''UPB legal/administrative data'''.
# 
# UPB's research services is obliged to check your AZAP budget form. So contact them as early as possible in the application process and send them the '''XML file''' from easy-Online to correct UPB data. Contacts can be found  [https://www.uni-paderborn.de/zv/2-2 '''here'''].
# 
# Ask them to provide you with a '''project account number''' as this needs to go into the AZAP.
# 
# Reserve time for the signature and submission process carried out by the research service center before the deadline is reached. (They need to get legal signatories to sign the AZAP in paper form (which they may want you to provide via in-house mail in the first place, i.e. more additional time needed) and a hard copy must be sent off to the granting authority on time.)

==== '''Zuwendungsbescheid''' ====  

===== Check List =====
# A funding announcement ('Drittmittelanzeige') must be published on FIS (via [mailto:nadine.jochimsen@uni-paderborn.de Nadine]). 
# 
# The project account (from the proposal phase) must be activated and access in MACH must be applied for (via [mailto:mone@upb.de Simone]).
# 
# The consortium agreement provided by the coordinator must be checked by one of UPB's legal advisors; the research service will tell us whom to contact for each proposal (often assigned on the basis of the granting authority).
#

a) Erfindungen/Schutzrechtsanmeldungen und erteilte Schutzrechte, die vom Zuwendungsempfänger oder von am Vorhaben Beteiligten gemacht oder in Anspruch genommen wurden sowie deren standortbezogene Verwertung (Lizenzen u.a.) und erkennbare weitere Verwertungsmöglichkeiten.

c) Wissenschaftliche und/oder technische Erfolgsaussichten nach Projektende (mit Zeithorizont) - u.a. wie die geplanten Ergebnisse in anderer Weise (z.B. für öffentliche Aufgaben, Datenbanken, Netzwerke, Transferstellen etc.) genutzt werden können. Dabei ist auch eine etwaige Zusammenarbeit mit anderen Einrichtungen, Firmen, Netzwerken, Forschungsstellen u.ä. einzubeziehen.
d) Wissenschaftliche und wirtschaftliche Anschlussfähigkeit für eine mögliche notwendige nächste Phase bzw. die nächsten innovatorischen Schritte zur erfolgreichen Umsetzung der Ergebnisse. == Access for external people ==

Both for the main repository and separate per-project repositories, there should be a guest IMT account for everybody who needs access. When it's ready, send the details to infrastructure@dice-research.org.

== Papers in SVN ==

To ensure that your paper appears on the website, please follow this steps:

# Make sure your paper appears on [https://www.bibsonomy.org/user/dice-research Dice Bibsonomy page] and is tagged with `dice` or `simba` tags, if not:
## Make sure you've [https://wikis.uni-paderborn.de/dice/Paper_writing#Updating_Bibsonomy added] your paper to bib file
## Make sure you've [https://wikis.uni-paderborn.de/dice/Paper_writing#Upload_to_Bibsonomy uploaded] new bib file to bibsonomy
## Make sure your publications either use your name, or have your `publicationTag` used on the website
# Make sure website was recently deployed (check the time of latest commit on `master` branch)

Papers on the website are only updated during deployments, so even if you add your paper to bib file and publish it to bibsonomy - website _will not_ be updated automatically.  
You can either re-deploy website manually (only recommended if you have also done any changes to the website itself), or simply wait for automated re-deployment that happens on Sunday midnight.  
If you followed the steps above and your paper is _still_ not on website - please [https://github.com/dice-group/dice-website/issues open an issue].

For more info on deployments, see [https://github.com/dice-group/dice-website/wiki/How-to-deploy%3F deployment page] in this wiki.

wikitext: = Folders = * {{Sciebo|952841994|DICE open}} * {{Sciebo|952841988|DICE closed}} * There are more secret folders = Access = To get access to the corresponding shared resources, people need to be added to corresponing groups: * [https://uni-paderborn.sciebo.de/apps/contacts/circle/stXmnosv2DhY6JobiR6NKOrG3vHPmeN SHKs and WHBs] - add new employees and student assistants there * [https://uni-paderborn.sciebo.de/apps/contacts/circle/V9HEt5a5taD2eEiXYraT8A8t73QUB6z DICE Mitarbeiter] * [https://uni-paderborn.sciebo.de/apps/contacts/circle/KQqgEsrzVBfGgmmwPOWqrN5oegpr34h DICE Leads] = Rules for DICE folders = * Do not directly share the whole folder with new members. Instead, they should be added to corresponding Teams in Sciebo contacts: ** [https://uni-paderborn.sciebo.de/apps/contacts/circle/stXmnosv2DhY6JobiR6NKOrG3vHPmeN DICE open] ** [https://uni-paderborn.sciebo.de/apps/contacts/circle/stXmnosv2DhY6JobiR6NKOrG3vHPmeN DICE closed] * '''Do not create public links''' in "External shares". * If you need to share a subfolder with somebody in DICE or a student: ** It should be limited scope (a project folder, or a folder for a student). ** Use "Internal shares" and specify '''Sciebo account''' there, '''do not use "External shares" with e-mail'''. * If you need to share a subfolder with "federated cloud id"? Please contact infrastucture team first. = About = https://uni-paderborn.sciebo.de/ Nextcloud instance with documents, spreadsheets, presentations, forms etc. Available for UPB employees and students, and also for some other institutions in NRW. Documentation: * https://hilfe.uni-paderborn.de/Sciebo * https://docs.sciebo.de/en/docs/ = Usage = == Registration == https://sns-sp.sciebo.de/secure/de.php == Inviting external guests == Invite a guest: https://sns-sp.sciebo.de/secure/mysciebo/#:~:text=G%C3%A4ste%20einladen Guest login after registration: https://gast.sciebo.de/ [https://docs.sciebo.de/en/docs/getting-started/gaeste/#:~:text=The%20guest%20will%20only%20appear%20in%20the%20address%20book%20of%20the%20sharing%20dialogue%20the%20day%20after%20activation. The guest will only appear in the address book of the sharing dialogue the day after activation.] Share with a guest: add EXTERNAL link, use identifier ivan.ivanov@example.com'''@gast.sciebo.de''' Manage guests: https://sns-sp.sciebo.de/secure/mysciebo/index.php?mode=manage_guests Docs: https://docs.sciebo.de/en/docs/getting-started/gaeste/ == Expiration == Extend the expiration date: https://sns-sp.sciebo.de/secure/mysciebo/index.php?mode=renew_user_account == Local file syncronization client (optional) == '''Do not try to locally edit files which are expected to be edited in an online collaborative scenario (such as meeting notes).''' Install the file synchronization client on Debian or Ubuntu: apt install nextcloud-desktop, use https://uni-paderborn.sciebo.de/ as the server address. You can choose which directories to syncronize to your machine. = Backups = == Sciebo == [https://docs.sciebo.de/en/docs/faq/#:~:text=Do%20you%20make%20backups Do you make backups of my data? No] == DICE == We set up a regular backup process on `dice-sciebo-backup.cs` VM in UPB. VM itself has the usual backup for VMs enabled. If you have some other folders in Sciebo and you want them to be a part of this backup, share them to our technical Sciebo account by creating '''EXTERNAL''' read-only link for '''ID''' infrastructure@dice-research.org@gast.sciebo.de. = Notes = * Public links with Edit/Upload access for all visitors can only be created for directories, not single files. * Permanent links do not work with guest accounts. The answer from sciebo support: "bitte verwenden Sie den öffentlichen Link und sichern Sie ihn mit einem Passwort ab. Private Links funktionieren nur innerhalb ein und derselben Instanz" (ticket WWU#202211151215)
