title: ServerSetup
wikitext:
= Server Setup Notes =

== Checklist for new servers ==

* If server has a GPU check CUDA versions on [https://developer.nvidia.com/cuda-downloads?target_os=Linux&target_arch=x86_64&Distribution=Debian CUDA download page]
* Install managed debian
** request CUDA if GPU available
** request ports 80/tcp, 443/tcp open
** request sudo access for members of the dice-admins group
* Create symlink from /upb to directory on data disk
* Add server to infrastructure ansible inventory and run experiment servers playbook
* Add server to jupyterhub ansible inventory and run playbook
* Add server to booking spreadsheet and announce it is available
* Docker data directory is on the data disk

title: Social Media
wikitext:
== Twitter == === Why is dissemination important? === Dissemination is important to generate visibility. Sharing our research results, our papers and conference attendance publicly can have a number of benefits: more people become aware of us and our research group becomes better known; we have a larger pool of applicants for our job advertisements; your papers get more attention and thus perhaps more citations; especially in externally funded research projects, it is important to show research activity - just to name a few advantages. === I have something that could be interesting for social media, what do I have to do? === If you want to share content, let us know in [https://matrix.to/#/!IibXYWvdzjyzFbrcwx:chat.dice-research.org?via=chat.dice-research.org&via=matrix.org Matrix chatroom DICE Dissemination] or send a message to Franzi. You don't have to have a finished tweet, it's enough if you want to share an idea. Franzi usually takes care of the wording of the tweet and a fitting graphic. === What content is suitable for social media? === * '''Papers''' accepted at conferences * '''Software''' releases with nice features * '''Projects''' and interesting news * Contents listed at the DICE website: new '''demos''', paper '''awards''', new '''job''' positions * Ideally, one of your papers will generate several posts: 1. at the acceptance at the conference, 2. at the presentation at the conference, 3. at the publication after the conference. We are also happy to present your paper in more detail in a multi-part tweet, for which you must provide some information and a graphic. === I don't have a Twitter account yet, how can I get started? === * Don’t have a [https://twitter.com/ Twitter] account you want to use for work? Create one and follow [https://twitter.com/diceresearch @DiceResearch]. * Good news: There is already a community, you can [https://twitter.com/i/lists/1149236446198476800/members follow some of your colleagues]. * Good news again: As you are working on your tasks, you’ve probably already become an expert for others. Share your knowledge and connect with other researchers! * Don’t have contents? Don’t worry. ** Start with checking tweets of [https://twitter.com/diceresearch @DiceResearch] and '''like''' them if you like them. ** If you really like tweets, '''retweet''' them. ** If you really like tweets and have additional information, add a '''comment''' to the respective tweet or retweet as a '''quote''' and add contents. * '''Don’t want to use Twitter?''' No problem. If you have contents to publish, just collect the required data (see below) and post it in [https://matrix.to/#/!pYWYtDiuVVxvituoyi:chat.dice-research.org?via=chat.dice-research.org Matrix chatroom SocialMedia]. We will take care. === 10 Ideas for Twitter Content === To further expand our Twitter account @DiceResearch and grow our network, we need your input! Therefore, we would be happy if each of you prepares content for at least 2 tweets, so that we can regularly provide the account with interesting insights from the DICE Group. The tweets don't have to be "Twitter ready" yet, I'll do the editing of the tweet. Here are 10 ideas for content: *'''1. Project Introduction – #DICEprojects''' Briefly tell us about the research project you are working on. What are you researching? What are the goals? Are there any particularly interesting results? A logo or group photo for the tweet would also be great. *'''2. Papers – #DICEreadme''' Present one of your papers: What is it about? Where can you find the full paper? For whom is it particularly interesting? Ideally, you also have a graphic that arouses the interest of the reader. *'''3. Fun Facts – #DICEfunfact''' You encounter something in your research that is somehow curious, funny, special or interesting? Just the right thing for a #DICEfunfact! The target audience here is people interested in our research, but maybe not necessarily technical experts. Would you like an example from my research on self-tracking? Here you go: Did you know that the famous 10,000 steps you should walk a day is not a recommendation from health experts at all? The number comes from a Japanese advertisement for a pedometer from the 1960s, but has somehow become so established that it is considered the "key to healthy living." *'''4. University Life – #DICElife''' Often, only the "end products" are communicated to the outside world: Papers, project results, PhD theses. But it's also interesting to see how you get there: What do you find particularly exciting in your research area? What does your day-to-day work look like? How did you get into research? What do you particularly like about your job? Tell us something about yourself and your research, maybe even with a photo of yourself or your research group. *'''5. Conferences – #DICEontour''' You're on the road at a conference right now? Tell us about it: What kind of conference is it? What is the program like? What will you present? A must-have is of course a nice tourist photo from the respective university or city where the whole thing takes place 😊 *'''6. Events''' Is there an event in your research project that is also open to interested parties, e. g. a lecture, a citizen science events or a workshop? Promote the event with the necessary information: What kind of event is it? When and where will it take place? How can I register? *'''7. “Scientific holidays”''' Whether it's AI Day on July 16 or Pi Day on March 14, international "holidays" like these are a fun way to generate reach on Twitter. What curious holiday do you find and why does it fit with DICE? *'''8. Interactions''' Ask followers a question, whether it's a technical discussion or a request for an opinion or specific info. On Twitter, you can either ask an open question or start a mini-poll with up to four possible answers. *'''9. Twitter Trends''' Go with the flow: look at established hashtags on Twitter, maybe there is something DICE can contribute to #MotivationMonday or #WisdomWednesday? 🤔 *'''1o. Optimization of DICE-Memability''' We all need a little fun from time to time - Why not put your creativity into creating memes? It's easy, e. g. with https://imgflip.com/memegenerator and even fun, really! Less visual, but just as fun, is a Chuck Norris joke in line with our research ( talk to Axel for examples 😅). === How do I create a social media post? === Good news is, you don't have to write the finished post, Franzi will take care of that. But you are welcome to prepare it as far as you can. * '''Who''' should do it? ** '''Papers''': Best would be the first author (others possible, e.g. if first author is not in our group) ** '''Projects''', '''jobs''', '''demos''': Respective leads ** '''Software''': Respective developers * Get a '''link''' to your '''main content'''. That provides useful information for your readers. ** For '''papers''' it could be the '''DOI-link''' (starting with ''doi.org/…'') of the published paper. It is typically provided on publisher websites. ** For '''papers''' that could also be the '''preprint PDF''' listed on [https://dice-research.org/publications/ dice-research.org/publications]. Use the paper link starting with ''papers.dice-research.org/…''
To create such a link, check "dice.bib contents" on the wiki page [[Paper writing]].
Important: Please check if preprints are allowed! ** For '''papers''', it could also be a link to your slides. You can use the SVN like described in [[Paper writing]] and add a suffix "''-slides-public.pdf''" ([https://papers.dice-research.org/2021/ICSC2021_ReCoDa/Relicensing-Combined-Datasets-ReCoDa-slides-public.pdf example]) ** For '''software''', it could be a release page on GitHub, like [https://github.com/dice-group/tentris/releases/tag/1.1.0 Tentris 1.1.0] or [https://github.com/dice-group/Squirrel/releases/tag/0.4 Squirrel 0.4]. ** For '''project''' updates, it could be news on the project website. You can also create a blog entry listed on [https://dice-research.org/news/ DICE news] on our website. * Start the '''tweet''' with a nice opener, maybe: ** A '''question''' which you answer in your work, e.g. “How to …? Check our paper …” ** An important '''result''' of your work, e.g. “There is a new state-of-the-art in …” ** The '''title''' of your work (easiest and quickest solution) * Add '''mentions''' for [https://twitter.com/diceresearch @DiceResearch], your co-authors, co-workers, conference accounts, conference heads (organising persons). * Check good '''hashtags'''. They should not be overused/generic (e.g. #data) and not too specific (e.g. #xmlgraphcompressionrules). You can check hashtag usage at [https://twitter.com/search-advanced Twitter advanced search]. * Add an '''image''' to add visual data. For papers, you could use one of your already prepared images from your article. === Twitter Tools === * [https://twitter.com/search-advanced Twitter advanced search] * Search also for retweets: [https://twitter.com/search?q=graphs%20(from%3ADiceResearch%20include%3Anativeretweets)&f=live graphs (from:DiceResearch include:nativeretweets)] (does not include all retweets) == DICE accounts == * DICE at '''Twitter''': [https://twitter.com/DiceResearch DiceResearch] (to be retweetet, mention @DiceResearch in your tweets) * DICE at '''Mastodon''': [https://mastodon.social/@diceresearch DiceResearch] (to be retweetet, mention @diceresearch in your tweets) * DICE at '''Facebook''': [https://www.facebook.com/DiceUPB DiceUPB] (is currently no longer used) * DICE at '''YouTube''': [https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCDshdIaiXqwZsQ4Gl_70OMA/ channel] (is currently no longer used) == Resources == * {{Sciebo|952858416|Dissemination document}}

title: Student assistants
wikitext:
=== Getting a student assistant === * You can hire students to get support for programming tasks, for research projects or for teaching. * Under [[Hiring students|Hiring student assistants]] (SHK/WHB), you find information about advertising the job as well as about negotiating and applying for/extending/terminating a contract. === Duties of the supervisor === * Working hours ** A student assistant can have up to 19 working hours per week. The lower limit is determined by the maximum hours you can work while staying below the BAföG earning limit beyond that students receive less BAföG money (see also minijob ceiling for contract planning [[Hiring_students#Hire_a_student|here]]). ** The weekly working hours should be taken into account when evaluating the performance of a student. * Tasks ** The supervisor is responsible for assigning enough tasks to the student assistant so that he/she has a sufficient workload to fulfill the contract. ** If the supervisor is running out of tasks for the student, the lead group should be asked for further tasks. ** Make sure the first 8-10 weeks of first-time student assistants involve enough programming tasks to see whether the student performs well enough to continue working at DICE (see [[Hiring_students#Hire_a_student|contract termination]]). * Commitments ** The supervisor is (together with the student assistant) responsible for the request, renewal or termination of a contract (info [[Hiring_students#Hire_a_student|'''here''']]). ** The supervisor is responsible for informing the student assistant about his/her vacation entitlement. ** The supervisor is responsible for notifying the student assistant in a timely manner that remaining vacation days expire by the end of the contract or by March 31 of the following year (whichever is applicable). ** When a contract ends or is renewed, the student assistant must have used the complete number of vacation days he/she is entitled to. ** To start an extension, the student assistant should not have more than 10 hours missing in his/her time sheets. * Time sheets ** The student assistant has to submit a time sheet for each month (Annual templates and guidelines can be found [https://www.uni-paderborn.de/zv/4-3/mindestlohngesetz-arbeitszeitaufzeichnung here].). ** The time sheet must be checked by the supervisor and signed by the supervisor and the student. ** The signed time sheet is uploaded by the supervisor here: _SVN_UPB_closed\organization\Hilfskraefte_Stundenzettel ** The file name should be formatted as follows: Lastname_Firstname _Month.year (If you have more than one first name, please enter only the first one). === Duties of student assistants === * Tasks ** The supervisor should assign tasks. Only the times at which the student is working on these tasks can be counted as working time. ** If a student is running out of tasks, he/she should inform his/her supervisor ASAP to get a new task. * Time sheets (https://www.uni-paderborn.de/zv/4-3/mindestlohngesetz-arbeitszeitaufzeichnung/) ** Time records have to be filled out for each month with the times at which the student worked on the tasks (Annual templates and guidelines can be found [https://www.uni-paderborn.de/zv/4-3/mindestlohngesetz-arbeitszeitaufzeichnung here].). ** They have to be submitted during the first half of the next month to the supervisor. ** They should contain the single table for the month as well as the overview (including the carryover from the last months). * Contract extension ** An extension takes 6 weeks for SHK and 8 weeks for WHB/WHK. The student assistant should talk to his/her supervisor ~7 (SHK)/ ~9 (WHB/WHK) weeks __before__ the end of his/her contract about the extension. === Vacations === Like every employee, students assistants should take vacations. The supervisor should keep track of the vacations and make sure that if a student leaves, they have used the complete amount of available vacations. ====Request a vacation==== The process of a student applying for vacations is different to other employed personal and defined as follows: # The student should ensure that they have enough vacation left. Students can only use vacation time from their current (or previous) contracts. (Exceptions might be possible in special cases, if the contract should be extended in the future and the supervisor agrees on the exception) # The student "applies" for vacations by writing to their supervisor, e.g., via mail or in the chat. This application has to be done in a written way and has to contain the exact duration of the vacations. The answer of the supervisor has to be in a written form as well, so that both sides have proof what has been agreed on. # The student marks the vacations in the time sheet by writing down the hours that they would have worked and write "vacation" in the column "Bemerkungen / Notes". ====Calculate your vacation days==== The following table is provided by the Human Resources Department of UPB (see also [https://www.uni-paderborn.de/fileadmin/zv/4-3/Mindestlohn/Urlaub-ZV.pdf here]) and should be used. [[Datei:Screenshot 2024-06-24 103627.png]] Although the contract of a student is on an hourly basis, the vacation time is calculated in days according to the table above. Given that an employee would get 20 days per year (v) and the year has 52 weeks of working days (w), the vacations ratio (vr) can be calculated as follows. 
v = 20d = 240h
w = 52 * 5d = 250d
vr = v / w = 20d / 250d = 0.08
Based on this ratio, the vacations per month can be calculated. For example, a student has a contract with 19h per week. In January 2019, he would have an expected work time of w=87.4h. During this month (or any other month within his contract), he could take v = 0.08 * w = 0.08 * 87.4h = 6.992h vacations. Note that according to the table above, a student assistant can take only half of their yearly vacations within the first half of the year although they may have a contract for a full year. === Illness === If a student assistant gets sick, the [[Illness|process]] is the same as for other employees. However, the [https://hobbitdata.informatik.uni-leipzig.de/dice-website/wiki/2022-12-01-illness-forms/Muster%20f%C3%BCr%20EAU%20neu%2001.08.2022%20englisch.pdf sick note] should be sent to '''krankmeldungen-hk@zv.upb.de''' instead. === Timesheets === Every student assistant is required to fill out timesheets on a monthly basis. Every month the student must create a PDF file with the spreadsheet, sign it, and send the signed file to his/her supervisor. In this section we briefly explain the basics of how to fill the timesheet and which fields the student is supposed to fill. Note that the university provides a more detailed instructions manual in [https://www.uni-paderborn.de/fileadmin/zv/4-3/Mindestlohn/MiLoG-Kurzbeschreibung_Nov2024.pdf German] or in [https://www.uni-paderborn.de/fileadmin/zv/4-3/Mindestlohn/MiLoG-Kurzbeschreibung_Nov2024_en.pdf English]. The timesheet for 2025 is [https://www.uni-paderborn.de/fileadmin/zv/4-3/Mindestlohn/MiLoG_2025_v1.7.xlsx here], but beware that the format changes every year and that new spreadsheets will be listed [https://www.uni-paderborn.de/zv/4-3/mindestlohngesetz-arbeitszeitaufzeichnung here]. '''Filling the timesheet'''
'''''Please note you are only allowed to change the yellow-framed cells''''' as the spreadsheet automatically computes the number of hours it expects the student to work each month based on the ''Stunden/Woche'' (hours per week) entry specified in the ''Stundennachweis'' sheet. # Fill in your personal details and your contract details in the starting page (Stundennachweis). In this sheet, you only need to edit the fields show in the image below. You can use the formula [https://wikis.uni-paderborn.de/dice/Student_assistants#Calculate_your_vacation_days above] to calculate your vacation days.
[[Datei:Start-page-timesheets.png|keine|none]] #
  • Fill in your daily working time in the month you're currently considering. Each day you work, record your start and end working time in the timesheet. This includes your vacations and sick leave. In the image below, you can see an example of how to fill the sheet in 3 different cases.
    • *Case 1: You worked on Days 1 and 2. You state the start and end working times, along with any pauses you had. Please note the maximum amount of consecutive hours you are allowed to work without a pause, as well as the maximum number of hours per day. These guidelines are mentioned in the ''Stundennachweis'' sheet of the spreadsheet. *Case 2: You were on sick leave on Day 3. You mark the hours as '''Urlaub/Krankheit (U/K)''' and add the Sick Leave comment. *Case 3: You were on vacations on Day 4. You mark the hours as '''Urlaub/Krankheit (U/K)''' and add the Vacations comment. [[Datei:Month-entry-timesheets-red.png|keine|none]] #
  • Create the PDF file in '''''landscape''''' mode with the Stundennachweis sheet and the respective Month.
    '''''Your PDF file should only have 2 pages!''''' If the month sheet is not fitting in one page, you can scale it down to 80% in the printing options or until it does fit. You can also disregard the overflow of the guidelines of the Stundennachweis sheet.
    • # Sign it. You can sign it digitally or print the PDF file, sign it, and then scan it again with your signature. # Submit the signed PDF file to your supervisor. '''Special case:''' If you've been employed since the previous year, you need to insert the last year's difference in the January timesheet. The cell is highlighted by the text in red "<-Ersatzzeiten hier eintragen" and you only need to fill it in this case! Below is an example of what the PDF might look like: [[Datei:Example-pdf-2-1.png|keine|none]] [[Datei:Example-pdf-2-2.png|keine|none]]

title: TLS
wikitext: == Managed servers and VMs == All managed VMs are automatically provisioned with a TLS certificate that includes all DNS names for that VM. These will be automatically renewed once they near expiry. These certificates are stored in /etc/ssl/private/irb-managed/. Additionally, symlinks to the fullchain and private key are made available at /etc/ssl/private/.{pem,key} for compatibility reasons. In addition, we provide monitoring for certificate health of hosts that are flagged as webservers. The following services are automatically reloaded when certificates change: * nginx.service * apache2.service If you'd like to trigger custom logic when certificates are updated, we suggest setting up * a systemd.path(5) unit that monitors changes to files in /etc/ssl/private/irb-managed that you're interested in * a systemd.service(5) containing the actions you'd like to invoke, triggered by the path unit For technical reasons, we suggest waiting a few seconds after receiving such an update notification before triggering the reload. This ensures that your software has a consistent view of these files. The exact action that will need to be invoked to reload certificates without downtime will vary based on your software. If your software runs in a systemd unit, the specific mechanism that your vendor provides will usually be exposed as the `ExecReload=` directive in its service unit, which can be invoked via `systemctl reload .service`.

'''L.079.05630''' == Exercises == * '''{{Sciebo|952848216|The teaching meeting folder}}''' provides current information. * We are using Jupyter notebooks for the exercises. Therefore, we have to prepare tasks and solutions in Java. * Jupyter videos/screencasts on how to create exercises are available in {{Sciebo|956580336}} === Creating exercises === To create a series of exercises (called ''assignments'' in Jupyter), you can choose one or both of the options: * Create files in your IDE. This is more comfortable for programming. * Create files in Jupyter. This is more direct. Both options contain 3 types of data: * Instructions for the students in markdown * The Java solution for the task * Tests for the solutions and the points for correct test runs. Each series (a.k.a. Jupyter assignment) sums up to '''24 points'''. ==== IDE ==== To clone the Java/Maven template for a series, you can use this command:
git clone -b java-template git@github.com:dice-group/nbgraderutils.git SemanticWeb_Series_XX ==== Jupyter ==== * Our Jupyter dev instance at '''https://diceapp.cs.upb.de:55555''' contains exercise templates in the ''source'' folder. * To edit your series, login with nbgadmin and the password upbdicenbg. * Test accounts are nbgtesta,nbgtestb,nbgtestc and also use the password upbdicenbg. === Upload your files === Finally, please upload your files to the [https://svn-serv.cs.uni-paderborn.de/datascience/teaching/2019_ss/LectureSemanticWeb/exercises/ UPB SVN]. * Java: Add the '''src folder''' as well as your '''pom.xml'''. * Jupyter notebooks: Add your '''ipynb files'''. You can copy the code by selecting the files in Jupyter and click on the 'Edit' button. == Administration: Live system students == * For admins (Adrian, Michael): Port 5555, datascienceupbnbg * [https://svn-serv.cs.uni-paderborn.de/datascience/teaching/2019_ss/LectureSemanticWeb/exercises/Backup/info.txt Backup] (Adrian)

title: Time Records
wikitext:
== Why do timesheets have to be filled out?== In many research projects, the funding body requires timesheets to be kept on the work in the project. It is important that these are filled out and archived carefully, as the documents can be checked in the event of an audit and, in the worst case, funding may have to be returned if it is not clear what work was carried out for the project in question. == Where can I find the timesheet template? == Paderborn University provides templates for the timesheets for the current year under [https://www.uni-paderborn.de/zv/2-3/formulare-und-merkblaetter this link] (only available from the university network). If you are not sure which template is the right one, please ask your supervisor or the coordinator of the project you are funded by. == What is important when filling out the timesheet? == * The maximum limits of the Working Hours Policy and the Working Hours Act must be observed. Accordingly, working hours of more than 10 hours per day are not permitted. * Hours recorded on weekends and public holidays are not permitted. * Tip: We recommend recording the average contractual working time per week. Overtime cannot be claimed with the Granting Authority. * Absences (e. g. vacation, illness, parental leave, maternity leave) are to be indicated with the working time "0" and marked with the keyword "absent" / "abwesend". You do not have to give the exact reason, it is sufficient to describe the day as “absent”. Tip: Make sure that your absences in the timesheet are absolutely identical with the leaves and days off that you reported to the Human Resources Department. * For the job description (“Tätigkeitsbeschreibung”), rough information is sufficient, e. g. you can simply enter the work package you have worked on (if in doubt, ask your supervisor or coordinator of the project you are working for). You should also enter all project events, e.g. colloquia, summer schools, meetings, retreats... * At 100% workload, the weekly working time is equivalent to 39 hours and 50 minutes. Make sure that these times are adhered to. * If the scope of work is lower, the weekly working time is reduced accordingly. If you work part-time on the project, make sure that your working days (i. e. which you report work for in the timesheet) match those specified in your employment contract.
[[Datei:Example Timesheet SAIL.png|gerahmt|zentriert|Here you can see an example of a working week entered in the timesheet for the SAIL project.]] == What happens with timesheets completed? == * A separate form must be used for each employee and student assistant and for each month. (See the tabs with the individual months at the bottom of the document). Please always enter the working hours for the respective month and print them out at the beginning of the following month. Then sign the timesheet and submit it to Axel or your supervisor for signature. Ask your supervisor or project coordinator who collects and archives the completed and signed timesheets. If needed the administration can request them.

title: Time records
wikitext:
== Time records for third-party funded projects == 

1) Please allocate your hours per week evenly over the available working days until the end of May. If you work part-time, try to choose the same day(s) per week for your working hours.

2) Don't add any extra hours or hours on weekends and bank holidays (dates in red).

3) Add any vacations/sick leaves/ etc. you took via InfAI by allocating the planned hours to the corresponding row under 'Abscences'. Synchronize this info with the data Simone (in Cc) has.

4) Add a brief list of tasks performed and the WP(s) they are related to. If you are not aware of the project tasks so much, ask for feedback from your supervisor.

Btw, this info will also be binding for our reports later. So if WPs are not so definite, choose more than one. So we'll remain flexible to some extent.

5) Check the basic personal and contractual information on the data sheet and alter if necessary.

6) When you sign, date each monthly timesheet with a date of the following month.

We need the timesheets signed digitally and on paper. You can send them to Simone at the address below. Please check them with Simone and your supervisor before signing.

title: Travel
wikitext: ==UPB Business Travel (Dienstreisen)== A business trip is any event that takes place outside Paderborn University. For example, a conference, a project retreat, a summer school, a project meeting, a workshop ... It does not matter whether the event takes place in Germany or abroad. === '''How to get your business trip financed''' === *'''Agree with''' your project lead or '''supervisor''' about you travel plans. *Clarify if '''budget''' is available and costs are eligible in this project (e.g. some projects don't foresee trips to conferences and fairs like Eurostar). ** (1) '''Employed on third-party funded projects:''' Your business trip must '''always''' be financed by the same '''project''' your position is financed from in the '''month you travel''', so check your current as well as follow-up employment contract for the project you are financed from. ** (2) '''Employed on university funded projects ('Landesstellen'):''' Your business trip can be financed by '''any''' '''project''' that your trip is relevant for and that you acknowledge in your paper, provided the project has money. **Note that some projects (often national third-party funding) require prior approval of travels outside of Europe from the funding authority. Speak to DICE research management. *Provide travel details [https://uni-paderborn.sciebo.de/f/952866777 here], especially a travel purpose for auditing and reporting purposes (how is your participation in the event relevant to the project that pays your trip?). *Once the project that pays for your trip is decided, ensure this project is also appropriately acknowledged in your publication, presentation and/ or poster. '''Project acknowledgements''' can be found [https://wikis.uni-paderborn.de/dice/Paper_writing#4.1_Acknowledgements here]. === '''How to get your business trip approved''' === Get '''prior approval''' ("Dienstreisegenehmigung") from UPB administration. Only when approved, expenses can be claimed and accident insurance coverage is given. 1. Fill out the business travel '''application form''' of UPB ([https://www.uni-paderborn.de/fileadmin/zv/4-1/reisekosten/intern/Antrag_auf_Genehmigung_einer_Dienstreise_Stand_24.06.26.pdf download here]). (''Please note that these forms are sometimes updated by UPB. Make sure that you always use the latest version.'') 2. Sign it. Either * digitally, or * print, sign and scan it again since you need the PDF 3. Add one of the following: * Invitation to the event * Acceptance notification of a paper or similar * Preliminary agenda or program 4. Merge everything into a single PDF file. [https://manpages.ubuntu.com/manpages/bionic/man1/pdfunite.1.html pdfunit] is an easy way to do that on the command line (linux): pdfunite file1.pdf file2.pdf ... output.pdf. If you face problems with the PDF of the application form (e.g., "Could not merge encrypted files") you can easily fix that by opening the PDF with Chrome and print it as image. 5. Send it to Simone via e-mail. Once Axel has signed it, it will be sent to the Travel Expenses Office who approve your form or may reject it if incomplete. Further information may be required. Make sure to submit all documents '''as early as possible''' as the individual steps (Axel's signature, processing at the Travel Expenses Office, handling rejections, internal mail) can take time. Attending an '''online event'''? No travel application is required. Costs are claimed by submitting a reimbursement form ("Kostenerstattung"). === '''Things to remember when travelling for UPB''' === *For costs incurred outside of Germany, UPB's '''VAT number''' (Umsatzsteuer-ID) must always be stated: '''DE 811209907'''. *Make sure '''invoices''' are issued to the university (i.e. billing address: Paderborn University - Fürstenallee 11 - 33102 Paderborn). *When high expenses are incurred in advance, you can request an advance payment from the university via ([https://www.uni-paderborn.de/fileadmin/zv/4-1/reisekosten/intern/Antrag_auf_Gewaehrung_eines_Abschlages_Stand_12.03.26.pdf this form]. *A '''risk form''' may be needed. The form and further information can be found here: [http://uni-paderborn.agu-hochschulen.de/index.php?id=1123 AGUM] *For non-EU nationals, check your '''visa''' requirements for travelling within and outside of the '''Schengen area'''. More information can be found [https://europa.eu/youreurope/citizens/travel/entry-exit/non-eu-nationals/index_en.htm here]. *Please add your absence to the "DICE group office absence" '''calendar'''. === '''Costs that can be covered by UPB''' === *By default, only economy class can be selected for '''transportation''' according to the [https://recht.nrw.de/lmi/owa/br_text_anzeigen?v_id=25020220105124746070 Travel Expenses Act of the state of North Rhine-Westphalia]. *There is a maximum limit for '''hotel''' costs. You can find an overview [https://www.uni-paderborn.de/fileadmin/zv/4-1/reisekosten/AKEVO_Saetze_ab_01.01.26.pdf on this site]. If there is no cheaper accommodation available, higher costs may be acceptable. We recommend to ask for prior approval from the Travel Expenses Office of UPB or reasons must be given at expense claim stage (e.g. document availability of hotels and their prices). A tip: For some hotels there are more attractive UPB company rates if you use a special link. You can find an overview here (only accessible from the university network): [https://www.uni-paderborn.de/en/zv/4-1/dienstreisen-1/dienstreisen-stichwortverzeichnis/hotelbuchungen Booking Links]. === '''How to promote your research activities on your business trip''' === *Send Franzi photos of your trip (via Element Chat or email) so that she can use them for social media posts. Preferably a photo of you presenting / of you in front of your poster, or in front of the conference building, a group photo if you are on site with several colleagues.... Especially for research projects, it can be mandatory to disseminate research activities *The group and especially Simone are very happy if we receive a postcard from your travels! :) === '''How to claim your costs from UPB''' === *You submit a '''travel expense claim''' to the Travel Expenses Office ([https://www.uni-paderborn.de/fileadmin/zv/4-1/reisekosten/intern/Reisekostenrechnung_Stand_24.06.26.pdf download here]), including: (1) the approved business travel application form and (2) original invoices and receipts for all travel expenses you wish to claim. (''Please note that these forms are sometimes updated by UPB. Make sure that you always use the latest version.'') *Assemble everything neatly and submit all documents via the in-house mail to the Travel Expenses Office. Usually, it only takes a few days to get the refund. *Another important note: Business trip expense reports are still sent to the administration by internal mail. Occasionally, envelopes get lost. It is advisable to scan receipts that cannot be replaced before submitting them to the secretariat. This way, they can be resubmitted if lost. *After you have been reimbursed for your expenses, enter the total amount of your business trip in our [https://uni-paderborn.sciebo.de/f/952866777 DICE Travels] overview. === '''How to claim your costs as a non-employee or external student''' === *'''People who are not employed or are not registered as students at Paderborn University''' can also take part in business trips financed by DICE projects. *They '''do not''' submit a business trip application before the business trip. *However, Axel must issue written authorization (i.e. email suffices) in advance stating why this business trip is necessary on behalf of UPB and which cost items (as usual or just single items like transportation or so) should be covered by UPB. *There is '''no insurance coverage''' for the person travelling. *After the business trip, they submit a travel expense claim as usual. === '''Summary of common pitfalls''' === A refund may be rejected partly or in total if specific conditions are not met. *Verify again whether the final publication of your paper includes an acknowledgment of the project that pays your travel. *Verify again whether your travel is paid from the project you are financed from. *Make sure you have prior official approval for making the trip from UPB administration (not just from your supervisor, DICE research management or the DICE secreatriat). Official approval is your application form for business trips signed and stamped by UPB administration. *Make sure that the approval also agrees on the way of transport you have chosen (e.g., short flights may not be covered) *Check your visa status and whether you can enter/exit all countries on your travel route. *''[can be extended by further experience]'' == Resources == *[https://www.uni-paderborn.de/zv/4-1/dienstreisen-1/dienstreisen-stichwortverzeichnis A-Z information] about Business travels at UPB *[https://www.uni-paderborn.de/fileadmin/zv/4-1/reisekosten/AKEVO_Saetze_ab_01.01.26.pdf Foreign daily allowance] (Auslandstagegeld, PDF) *[http://web3.hrs.de/?clientId=ZGVfX05SV0ZN Hotel Reservation Service (HRS)] *[http://www.bahn.de/bahncorporate bahn.business] *[https://www.uni-paderborn.de/fileadmin/zv/4-1/reisekosten/Leitlinien_fuer_umweltvertraeglichere_Dienstreisen_19.07.2023.pdf Sustainable Travel Guidelines]

title: Vacation
wikitext:
== Apply for leave ==

* Since spring 2024, it has been possible for all employees to apply for leave online via the ATOSS time recording tool (https://zeiterfassung.uni-paderborn.de/SES/html). This procedure is intended to replace the old procedure with paper forms. Please note: ATOSS is only accessible via the university network or via VPN. 
* Axel approves the leave directly in ATOSS. There you can see which vacation days you have applied for and whether they have already been approved. 
* Please add your absence to the "DICE group office absence" calendar
* Please note: The procedure described here applies to all academic staff. You can find information on applying for vacation days for student assistants here: https://wikis.uni-paderborn.de/dice/Student_assistants

== Available number of vacation days ==

* At ATOSS you can see how many vacation days you are still entitled to in the current year and how many you have already taken. See https://zeiterfassung.uni-paderborn.de/SES/html (only accessible via the university network or via VPN).

== Email absence message ==

* You can set an automatic response at the [https://serviceportal.uni-paderborn.de/ service portal] at User Selfcare -> Mailbox settings.

== Travel ==

Please ensure that you '''do not''' take university equipment with you on vacations, unless it is necessary. This includes:
* The laptop that you may have got from university
* The university key
* The key card for TP6

== Public holidays ==

* [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_holidays_in_Germany Wikipedia: Public holidays in Germany]
* Import to your calendar (ical): [https://www.schulferien.org/deutschland/ical/ schulferien.org]

== Resources ==

* {{UPB network link|https://zeiterfassung.uni-paderborn.de/SES/html|ATOSS Tool}}

title: Vault
wikitext: == Requirements == You need to have 2FA enabled in https://git.cs.uni-paderborn.de and be a member of {{IMT group|dice-secrets}}. == Usage == [https://vault.cs.uni-paderborn.de:8200/ui/vault/auth?with=oidc Vault UI]: use OIDC as the method, and '''dice as the role'''. [https://vault.cs.uni-paderborn.de Auxiliary overview UI] (uses IMT accounts): listing/searching for KV paths. It provides a list of all paths to which you have access and deep links to the corresponding secrets in the vault UI. * [https://vault.cs.uni-paderborn.de/oidc:oidc:dice.html] DICE page ** https://vault.cs.uni-paderborn.de:8200/ui/vault/secrets-engines/kv/kv/list/fg/ds/dice/ a namespace for our own secrets Handy login link: https://vault.cs.uni-paderborn.de:8200/ui/vault/auth?redirect_to=%2Fvault%2Fsecrets%2Fkv%2Fkv%2Flist%2Ffg%2Fds%2Fdice%2F&with=oidc == Details of IRB setup == * a `dice-infrastructure` policy that grants access to certain paths * a `dice` role that binds the `dice-secrets` gitlab groups to the `dice-infrastructure` policy * a section on the overview UI listing paths applicable to your role. * Because secrets in vault are always JSON objects, we have standardized on storing the primary value of a secret at the `value` key within that JSON object. == See also == [[IPMI]]

title: VirtualMachines
wikitext: * DICE ** Main contact: '''Infrastructure group''' and technical administratior (see [[Team]]) * IRB ** [https://cs.uni-paderborn.de/en/irb/dienstuebersicht/virtual-machines/ IRB VMs] (Requesting a VM, graphical access, backup, ...) ** vSphere client: https://vmc.cs.uni-paderborn.de/ * Configuration ** Check, if vmware tools are installed: vmware-toolbox-cmd -v =Requesting a new VM= ==Types of VMs== ===IRB managed (Debian)=== '''This is the preferred option''' unless you have specific reasons to choose something else. * IRB manages the installation, updates, monitoring, and upgrades (by request) * IMT accounts * OS: only Debian ====Important steps after acquiring the VM==== * Set up the home directories to be located in the large disk partition: sudo ln -s /data/upb /upb && sudo mkdir /data/upb * Create your home directory: sudo mkhomedir_helper YOUR_IMT_USERNAME More information: [[IRB-managed]] ===Self-Installed=== '''This option should be avoided.''' If you still need something else, you need to provide a (short) explanation why IRB-managed Debian system would not work for your use case. You get a empty VM and are responsible for installing an OS of your choice. You should include the name of the OS you are planning to install in the mail. '''You will need to manage OS updates and upgrades by yourself. Otherwise, the VM will be shut down if the software would get outdated.''' ===Windows=== Contact IRB for the details. ==Naming your VM== It's a good idea to include a reference to your project and/or purpose of the VM in the hostname. Namespace is also shared with everyone else in the CS department, so it might be a good idea (but not mandatory) to start your name with dice-. The VM would be accessible by name.cs.uni-paderborn.de inside the UPB network. ==Resources== {| class="wikitable" |+ IRB VM resources |- ! Resource !! Default !! Maximum |- | CPUs || 2 || 64 |- | RAM || 4 GB || 256 GB |- | SSD || 30 GB || 2 TB |} If you request more than the default amount, you need to (briefly) specify why you need it. ==Template== Recipients: irb+ds@upb.de CC: infrastructure@dice-research.org Hello, we need a new VM for Name: Access for: dice-admins, OS: Needed Resources: 1 (v)CPU 4 GB RAM 30 GB HDD Ports which would be used inside UPB network: (Example: 8080/tcp, 1234/tcp [list all the ports which would serve services inside UPB network.]) Opened ports (IMT firewall): (Example: 80/tcp, 443/tcp [you need this only if you want the VM to be reachable from outside the UPB network on those ports.]) Additional Requirements: sudo access for members of the dice-admins group, Backups: Contacts: AdminC: Name: IMT Login: Group: Datascience TechC: Mailinglist: dice-infrastructure@lists.uni-paderborn.de Keep dice-admins in access list, unless there is a specific reason to remove that (in that case, send explanation to infrastructure@dice-research.org first). Please note that the AdminC has to be a permanent employee (you) and not a student assistent. It's also possible to ask for a clone (copy) of an existing VM. =Removing a VM= Do not need your VM anymore? If you are the administrative contact, just send another message: Recipients: irb+ds@upb.de CC: infrastructure@dice-research.org ... If the person responsible for the VM is not available, then send a message to infrastructure@dice-research.org explaining why the VM is not needed anymore and we will take care of removing it. =Automated reboots= IRB managed VMs automatically reboot for security updates and similar reasons. The process as mentioned at 2023-06-02 is: "Whenever a server needs to reboot, the administrative and the technical contact will be reminded after 1 and 5 days. After a week, the server will be rebooted if no one is working on it." It is suggested to use [https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/systemd-inhibit.html systemd-inhibit] if you need to disable automatic reboot. =GPUs= You can request a VM with a GPU. See also: https://wiki.cs.uni-paderborn.de/CSIPB/NVIDIA_GRID == torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: operation not supported == Check nvidia-smi -q | grep License. Try to restart nvidia-gridd.service or the VM. Contact IRB. =FAQ= ===I need a VM to deploy a long-running service.=== Use a IRB-managed VM or contact the infrastructure crew. ===I don't know how much Hardware I need.=== Start with Needed Resources: Standard configuration and request more resources for your VM when you need it. ===I need more resources.=== Write a mail to Recipients: irb+ds@upb.de CC: infrastructure@dice-research.org and ask them to increase the resource you require (CPU, RAM or Disk space). It is likely that they would need to restart your VM and they would ask you if it is okay to restart it. To speed things up, you can tell them that it is okay to restart it in your message. ===I requested a DFN X.509 Certificate, where is it located?=== See [[TLS]] ===I have no home directory at a IRB-managed Debian VM.=== Try sudo mkhomedir_helper USERNAME ===VM has no home directories=== They can be created with: sudo mkdir -p /upb/users/{a..z} sudo pam-auth-update --enable mkhomedir ===Figure out if VM has backups enabled=== "basically, if the directory /opt/commvault exists, backups are enabled" ===Upgrade to a newer OS version=== "the normal process is that we provide a new VM with the new Debian Release and you transfer the data from the old VM to the new one" ===Connection to open ports from the internet fails=== If a TLS connection does not (yet) have a proper TLS certificate, UPB ZIM firewall would drop all connections.
